strings.Почему это важно для названия Онфилогово: Why this matters for the name Onfilogovo
strings.Название деревни и именование человека п: The name of the village and the naming of the person follow the same possessive pattern: Onfilogovo is Onfilog's place, Anfilogov is Anfilog's man. Evgraf documentarily proves that such a transformation of a rare name really worked in living records, although it belongs to another period and locality.
strings.старший костюринский носитель формы Анфи: an older Kostyurino bearer of the form Anfilogov, possibly the previous generation of the same naming circle
strings.владелец одноимённого Острогина и возмож: owner of a like-named Ostrogino and a possible participant in the break-up of the neighbouring complex
strings.Стефан Яковлев сын Осколков: Stefan Yakovlev syn Oskolkov (Stefan, son of Yakov, Oskolkov)
strings.В 1567/1568 году передал Осипову монасты: In 1567/1568 he gave the Osipov Monastery the village of Ostrogino in the Yuryev stan, which he had previously bought from the Tsyzyrev brothers. Its identity with Stefanida's Ostrogino has not yet been proved.
strings.«Стефан Яковлев сын Осколков» разворачив: «Стефан Яковлев сын Осколков» ["Stefan, Yakov's son, Oskolkov"] unfolds as Stepan, son of Yakov, Oskolkov. Stefan is the church form of the name Stepan; Yakovlev syn is an explicit patronymic; Oskolkov is the family name. Thus the card loses none of the layers of the old formula.
strings.Он не основатель и не первый известный х: He is neither the founder nor the first known owner: he himself writes that he bought the village from Ivan and Matvei Tsyzyrev. His place in the chain is that of buyer and then donor to the monastery.
strings.Почему монастырский переход важен: Why the transfer to the monastery matters
strings.Если подтвердится тождество Острогина с: If the identity of Ostrogino with a village of Stefanida's complex is confirmed, the transfer to the monastery will explain why this part disappeared from the later inventory of the secular pomestyes of Starkov, Bulbin and Yurlov. For now this is a strong explanation, not a proven fact.
strings.Что акт говорит о семье: What the act says about the family
strings.Жена, дети и род упомянуты без имён толь: The wife, children and kin are mentioned without names only to renounce future claims. They must not be turned into invented profiles: the document establishes the existence of a family circle, but not its composition.
strings.Высокая уверенность: человек, полное имя: High confidence: the person, the full name, Ostrogino in the Yuryev stan, the purchase and the donation. Medium: he belongs to the same local circle as Nikolskoye Svechino. Low until a boundary check: this is precisely Stefanida's Ostrogino.
strings.один из братьев-продавцов одноимённого О: one of the selling brothers of the like-named Ostrogino
strings.Иван Тимофеев сын Цызырев: Ivan Timofeyev syn Tsyzyrev (Ivan, son of Timofei, Tsyzyrev)
strings.Сын Тимофея и брат Матвея; вместе с брат: Son of Timofei and brother of Matvei; together with his brother he sold Ostrogino to Stepan Oskolkov before 1567/1568.
strings.В акте два имени объединены формулой «Ив: In the act the two names are joined by the formula «Иван да Матвей, Тимофеевы дети» ["Ivan and Matvei, Timofei's children"]. This is not an editor's assumption: the plural patronymic directly makes Ivan a son of Timofei.
strings.Один отец, одно фамильное именование и с: One father, one family name and the joint sale of one votchina village form a direct fraternal formula. Here kinship is established more reliably than many later genealogical links on the card.
strings.На странице читается Цызырев. В других п: On the page the reading is Tsyzyrev. Other retellings have Tsyzarev, Tsuzyrev, Tsyzorev. Fluctuation in the unstressed vowels and in the difficult cluster -zyr- does not automatically create different families; each variant needs to be searched for separately.
strings.Акт называет целую «деревеньку Острогино: The act names a whole «деревеньку Острогино» ["little village of Ostrogino"] with forest, meadows and all the old appurtenances. But since the deed of purchase is not published here in full, it is unknown whether this was the whole village, a family share or a separate like-named holding.
strings.Ни отчество Иваново, ни фамилия Цызырев: Neither the patronymic of Ivan nor the surname Tsyzyrev contains the name Onfilog. His significance is indirect: the family's documents may lead to the earlier chain of ownership of the neighbouring land, but Ivan himself is not a candidate for the eponym.
strings.второй брат-продавец одноимённого Острог: the second selling brother of the like-named Ostrogino, independently known in Tver from 1540
strings.Матвей Тимофеев сын Цызырев: Matvei Timofeyev syn Tsyzyrev (Matvei, son of Timofei, Tsyzyrev)
strings.Сын Тимофея и брат Ивана. Веселовский не: Son of Timofei and brother of Ivan. Veselovsky independently records Matvei Timofeyevich Tsyzarev (Tsyzyrev) in Tver under 1540.
strings.Почему это особенно сильное имя: Why this is an especially strong name
strings.Редкое сочетание Матвей + отчество Тимоф: The rare combination Matvei + patronymic Timofeyevich + Tsyzyrev + Tver coincided in two independent publications: in this 1567/1568 deed of gift and in the Onomastikon with the date 1540. The probability of a chance namesake is small.
strings.Матвей был взрослым участником тверского: Matvei was an adult participant in the Tver landholding world already at roughly the time when Onfilogovo was first described. This places him in the immediate chronological circle of Stefanida Yurlova, although it does not make him her relative.
strings.Ономастикон называет человека, год и Тве: The Onomastikon names the person, the year and Tver, but not Ostrogino. The link of the Matvei of 1540 specifically with the village from the deed of gift is plausible on the basis of the full name, while the link of this village with Stefanida's Ostrogino still requires separate proof.
strings.Первичная проверка исправила роспись: A primary check corrected the listing
strings.На с. 191 братья владеют Острогиным толь: On p. 191 the brothers hold Ostrogino only in the new layer of the 1551–1554 survey. The old part names Timofei Chernyshev and Ushek Kudryavtsov; dating the Tsyzyrevs' holding to 1540 was a mistake. P. 234 confirms their father, Sholygino and Matvei's deed of purchase.
strings.Нужна полная статья о Матвее и Иване в п: What is needed is the full article on Matvei and Ivan in the scribal materials of 1540 and 1551: the size of the land, the neighbours, the name of the stream and the votchina formula. A single coincidence with Sadykovo, Ishkovo, Svechino or Voronino would decisively raise the probability of identity.
strings.отец двух прежних владельцев Острогина,: father of the two former owners of Ostrogino, a man of the eponym's generation
strings.Тимофей, отец Ивана и Матвея: Timofei, father of Ivan and Matvei
strings.Тимофей, отец Ивана и Матвея Цызыревых: Timofei, father of Ivan and Matvei Tsyzyrev
strings.Лично в данной не действует; отдельная с: He does not act personally in the deed of gift; a separate entry of the survey names him directly as Timofei Semyonovich, the former owner of Sholygino, who died before 1551–1554.
strings.Как человек появляется без собственной с: How a person appears without a line of his own
strings.Иван и Матвей названы «Тимофеевыми детьм: Ivan and Matvei are called «Тимофеевыми детьми» ["Timofei's children"]. The father's name is given twice in one shared grammatical form, so the existence of their father Timofei is a reliable inference from the source, not a family legend.
strings.Полное имя установлено первично: Full name established from a primary source
strings.С. 234 буквально называет «Тимофея Семен: P. 234 literally names «Тимофея Семенова сына Цузырева» ["Timofei Semyonov son Tsuzyrev"]. His given name, patronymic, family name, possession of Sholygino and fatherhood of Matvei and Ivan are now established.
strings.Ефимья, жена Семёна Цызырева, стоит в то: Yefimya, wife of Semyon Tsyzyrev, appears in the same old entry, so she may have been Timofei's mother. But there is no direct formula «мать его» ["his mother"]; the motherhood and the exact composition of the older generation are not proven.
strings.Тимофей владел Шолыгином в старом слое о: Timofei held Sholygino in the old layer of the description and died before the survey of 1551–1554. He belongs roughly to the generation of the unknown Onfilog, but this is chronological proximity, not kinship.
strings.Нет оснований заменять одно имя другим:: There are no grounds for substituting one name for the other: Timofei is a separate calendar name, while Onfilog is the stem of the toponym. Timofei matters as a possible holder of archival charters of the same landholding circle, but not as a candidate for the eponym.
strings.тверской боярин по прозвищу Свеча; вероя: Tver boyar nicknamed Svecha; probable progenitor of the Svechins and a possible key to the name Svechino
strings.Представитель тверского боярского круга: A member of the Tver boyar circle of the mid-15th century, from whom genealogies derive the Svechins. The coincidence of the nickname with the name of Nikolskoye Svechino gives rise to a hypothesis that the name of the centre derives from an owner, but no direct charter for this village has been found.
strings.Свеча здесь мирское прозвище Андрея Конс: Svecha here is the secular nickname of Andrei Konstantinovich, not a mention of a church candle. In the genealogical formula it is precisely this nickname that explains why the descendants were called Svechins.
strings.Название Свечино имеет ту же притяжатель: The name Svechino has the same possessive construction: Svech-in-o, the settlement of Svecha or of Svechin. If the family owned the place, the name could have become fixed after Andrei or one of his descendants. For now this is a linguistically and chronologically possible chain, but not one closed by documents.
strings.Свеча объясняет возможное происхождение: Svecha explains the possible origin of the name of the estate centre, but not that of the dependent village of Onfilogovo. The two names may preserve the memory of different people: the service owner of the centre and the local first settler of the village.
strings.Высокая уверенность относится к существо: High confidence applies to the existence of the Tver line of the Svechins and to the nickname Svecha; medium confidence to the matching era; low confidence to ownership of Nikolskoye Svechino specifically. Proof would require a pomestye, votchina or boundary charter naming the village.
strings.новоторжский землевладелец XVI века из р: 16th-century landowner of Novy Torzhok from the Svechin family
strings.Внук Андрея Свечи по родословной линии;: Grandson of Andrei Svecha in the genealogical line; a landowner of Novy Torzhok known from the Dvorovaya tetrad (Court Register) of the 1550s. He documents the presence of the Svechins near Tver uyezd in Stefanida's time, but not ownership of Nikolskoye Svechino.
strings.Матвей — личное имя, Федоров сын — отчес: Matvei is the given name, Fyodorov syn the patronymic, Svechin the family name derived from the nickname Svecha. This formula is already closer to a stable service surname than the single nickname of the progenitor.
strings.Новоторжские владения помещают семью в т: The Novy Torzhok holdings place the family in the Tver landholding world, not in some random distant uyezd. This makes a search for Svechin deeds reasonable, but administrative proximity by itself does not identify the estates.
strings.Связь с названием села: Connection with the name of the village
strings.Если Никольское Свечино было родовым или: If Nikolskoye Svechino was an ancestral or former holding of the Svechins, the charters of Matvei and his sons may record the transfer of the land to Ivan Yurlov. So far no line found contains both Matvei and Svechino.
strings.новоторжский помещик и участник тверских: Novy Torzhok pomeshchik and participant in Tver land surveys of the late 16th century
strings.Сын Матвея Фёдоровича; назван среди служ: Son of Matvei Fyodorovich; named among the service people in the Tver list of 1585. According to a genealogical reference, in 1580 he took part in describing the holdings of Simeon Bekbulatovich in Tver uyezd. There is as yet no direct connection with Nikolskoye Svechino or Onfilogovo.
strings.Почему это самый конкретный Свечин: Why he is the most concrete Svechin
strings.Пётр документирован не только родословно: Pyotr is documented not only by the genealogical scheme but also by the published Tver service list of 1585. He lived after the first description of Onfilogovo, so he could not have given the village its old name, but he may lead to the family archive and to former holdings.
strings.К концу XVI века Свечин выступает устойч: By the end of the 16th century Svechin functions as a stable family name. Its distant root is the nickname Svecha; it does not indicate a candlemaker's trade and is no proof of a church origin of the village.
strings.Что искать по нему: What to search for under his name
strings.Нужны описи земель, данные и купчие Петр: We need land inventories, deeds of gift and deeds of purchase of Pyotr and his father, especially those with the neighbours Pervitino, Romanovo, Voronino, Sadykovo or the Yurlovs. A match of at least two stable neighbours could link the family to our Svechino.
strings.Наличие Свечина в Тверском служилом спис: The presence of a Svechin in the Tver service list proves the person and the local service milieu, but not a right to the village of the same name. On this card he is marked as a search key, not as a former owner.
strings.сын реального Анфилофа XV века; участник: son of a real 15th-century Anfilof; participant in Kashin land deeds
strings.деревня Красникова, Жабенский стан Кашин: village of Krasnikova, Zhabensky stan of Kashin uyezd
strings.Около 1499—1505 годов был послухом купче: Around 1499–1505 he was a witness (poslukh) to a deed of purchase for the village of Krasnikova in Zhabensky stan of Kashin uyezd and signed it; later he himself wrote a land deed of purchase and again acted as a witness. His patronymic preserves the name of his father Anfilof of the relevant generation. No direct connection of the family with Nikolskoye Svechino, the Yurlovs or Onfilogovo has been found.
strings.Купчая около 1499—1505 годов заканчивает: The deed of purchase of around 1499–1505 ends the list of witnesses with the words «да Пешок Анфилофов сын Лодыгина» ["and Peshok Anfilofov son Lodygin"], and then states: «К сей купчей грамоте яз, Пешок, и руку свою приложил» ["To this deed of purchase I, Peshok, have set my hand"]. This is at once a given name, a patronymic, a family name and evidence of personal participation.
strings.Пешок — личное бытовое имя или прозвище;: Peshok is a personal everyday name or nickname; Anfilofov syn is a direct patronymic reference to his father Anfilof; Lodygin is the family name. In the name index the editors normalised the entry as «Лодыгин Пешок Анфилофов сын» ["Lodygin Peshok Anfilofov son"].
strings.Пешок был совершеннолетним участником зе: Peshok was already an adult participant in a land transaction around 1499–1505 and continued to act until 1515/1516. Consequently, his father Anfilof belonged to an earlier generation and could well have lived in the middle or second half of the 15th century, precisely when the name attested in 1539/1540 must have arisen.
strings.Почему это новый кандидат: Why this is a new candidate
strings.Прежние ранние носители имени были найде: Earlier bearers of the name had been found in Yaroslavl, Uglich, Ryazan and northern deeds. Here a real Anfilof is reconstructed within Kashin uyezd, part of the Tver historical-geographical and service world. This raises the regional significance of the trace, although Kashin and Tver uyezds remain different territories.
strings.Издатели связывают одного Пешка с тремя: The editors link one Peshok to three deeds: witness and signatory around 1499–1505; scribe of another deed of purchase around 1505–1510; witness in 1515/1516. This is not a random single OCR line but a person consistently active in the Kashin landholding milieu.
strings.Почему он ещё не основатель: Why he is not yet the founder
strings.Все известные действия относятся к Кашин: All known acts belong to Kashin uyezd and the Kalyazin deed collection. Not a single line names Nikolskoye Svechino, Onfilogovo, Khorvach volost or the Yurlovs. The patronymic proves the existence of Anfilof, but not his relocation, ownership, or founding of a Tver village.
strings.АСЭИ. Т. III. М.: Наука, 1964. № 169 и 1: ASEI (Acts of the Socio-Economic History of North-Eastern Rus). Vol. III. Moscow: Nauka, 1964. Nos. 169 and 174, pp. 179 and 189; name index, p. 551; additional editors' reference to Kalyazin book IV, No. 4, l. 1v. The full text of the last deed of 1515/1516 and the early ancestral holdings of the Lodygins should be checked: the appearance of Tver neighbours or the Yurlovs would raise the candidate.
strings.отец Пешка Лодыгина; имя восстановлено и: father of Peshok Lodygin; name reconstructed from a direct patronymic
strings.отец Пешка Анфилофова сына Лодыгина: father of Peshok Anfilofov syn Lodygin
strings.Кашинский уезд, земельно-актовый круг се: Kashin uyezd, the land-deed circle of the Lodygin family
strings.Самостоятельной строкой в купчей не назв: He is not named in a line of his own in the deed of purchase. The profile was created because the formula «Пешок Анфилофов сын Лодыгина» ["Peshok Anfilofov son Lodygin"] reliably attests the existence of a father Anfilof of an earlier generation. A connection with Tver Onfilogovo remains a hypothesis.
strings.Почему создан отдельный профиль: Why a separate profile was created
strings.Патроним на -ов сын сообщает реального о: A patronymic in -ov syn indicates a real father, not an abstract linguistic form. Therefore Anfilof is a separate historical person, although so far he is known only through his son.
strings.С высокой уверенностью доказаны личное и: The given name Anfilof and his fatherhood of Peshok are proven with high confidence. Peshok himself was active around 1499–1505 and later; consequently, the father belonged to an earlier generation.
strings.Полное именование «Анфилоф Лодыгин» прин: The full form «Анфилоф Лодыгин» ["Anfilof Lodygin"] is adopted as a convenient profile name after the son's family. The source gives no separate line with a surname form, patronymic, holding or place of residence of the father himself.
strings.Это ближайший найденный региональный сле: This is the closest regional trace found within the broad Tver historical-geographical circle, but not a proven eponym: no deed connects Kashin uyezd with Nikolskoye Svechino.
strings.Купчая оформлена как самостоятельная зап: The deed of purchase is set up as a separate Record PUB-ASEI3-1499-KASHIN-PESHOK-ANFILOFOV, which shows separately the directly named Peshok and the father reconstructed from his patronymic.
strings.сын реального Анфилога; участник рязанск: son of a real Anfilog; participant in a late-15th-century Ryazan boundary survey
strings.Рязанская земля, межа Петровичей и Яруст: Ryazan land, the boundary of Petrovichi and Yarustovo
strings.В разъезжей грамоте 1483—1503 годов назв: In a boundary charter of 1483–1503 he is named as a prince's man at the setting of a boundary in the Ryazan land. His patronymic directly preserves the name of his father Anfilog and confirms the existence of that name in the generation of the presumed eponym. There is no geographical or ownership connection with Tver Onfilogovo.
strings.Разъезжая 1483—1503 годов называет при м: The boundary charter of 1483–1503 names at the boundary survey «Антипу Анфилогова сына Феодотьевского» ["Antipa Anfilogov son Feodotyevsky"], a man of Prince Fyodor Vasilyevich of Ryazan. The editors' reading and the name index make it possible to separate the given name Antipa from the patronymic Anfilogov syn.
strings.Антипа — имя самого участника; Анфилогов: Antipa is the participant's own name; Anfilogov syn is a direct reference to a father named Anfilog; Feodotyevskoy is an additional family or ownership designation, given by the source in an old form. Consequently, the deed attests a second older 15th-century Anfilog, and does not present Antipa as a variant of the name Onfilog.
strings.Антипа был взрослым участником межевого: Antipa was an adult participant in a boundary survey no later than the beginning of the 16th century, so his father Anfilog belongs to an even earlier generation. Chronologically, this is exactly the layer in which the person who gave his name to the village, already existing in 1539/1540, could have lived.
strings.Что известно о положении: What is known about his position
strings.В акте Антипа назван человеком князя Фёд: In the deed Antipa is named as a man of Prince Fyodor Vasilyevich of Ryazan and took part in the official setting of a boundary. This shows another social milieu of the name: Anfilog's family could belong not only to a peasant household but also to a prince's service retinue. The exact status of the father himself is not reported.
strings.Почему это не тверской основатель: Why this is not the Tver founder
strings.Документ относится к Рязанской земле и н: The document belongs to the Ryazan land and does not contain Nikolskoye Svechino, the Yurlovs, Khorvach or Tver neighbours of Onfilogovo. The name and generation match, but not the geography or the chain of ownership; therefore Anfilog, father of Antipa, remains a control parallel rather than a candidate on the level of the Uglich or Kashin trace.
strings.Акты социально-экономической истории Сев: Akty sotsialno-ekonomicheskoy istorii Severo-Vostochnoy Rusi (Acts of the Socio-Economic History of North-Eastern Rus). Vol. III. Moscow: Nauka, 1964. No. 323a, p. 352; name index of the same volume. The editors dated the deed to the interval 1483–1503.
strings.отец Антипы; самостоятельный носитель им: father of Antipa; an independent 15th-century bearer of the name Anfilog
strings.Рязанская земля, княжеский служилый круг: Ryazan land, the prince's service circle
strings.Сам в разъезжей грамоте не действует, но: He does not act himself in the boundary charter, but Antipa's direct patronymic reliably attests a separate father named Anfilog. A separate profile was created by the same rule as for the father of Peshok Lodygin.
strings.Почему профиль принадлежит отцу, а не то: Why the profile belongs to the father and not only to the son
strings.В записи «Антипа Анфилогов сын» личное и: In the entry «Антипа Анфилогов сын» ["Antipa Anfilogov son"] the participant's given name is Antipa, while the form Anfilogov syn gives the name of another person, his father. The patronymic is evidence of kinship and allows a cautious separate profile of a historical person to be created.
strings.Отца звали Анфилог, а Антипа был его сын: The father was called Anfilog, and Antipa was his son. The name is attested not by a later surname or a guess from the name of the village, but by a direct grammatical form in a published deed.
strings.Антипа уже был взрослым княжеским челове: Antipa was already an adult prince's man between 1483 and 1503. His father belongs to an earlier generation of the 15th century, exactly the chronological layer in which the eponym of the settlement recorded in 1539/1540 could have lived.
strings.Почему имя особенно важно: Why the name is especially important
strings.Это раннее прямое доказательство мирског: This is early direct evidence of the secular use of the full form Anfilog. It shows the path from a given name to the patronymic Anfilogov syn; later a similar model could produce both a person's name and the name of a settlement in -ovo.
strings.Источник не называет самого отца отдельн: The source does not name the father himself in a separate line. His patronymic, holding, occupation, exact place of residence, and whether the form Feodotyevskoy applied to him or only to his son's name are unknown.
strings.Почему это не найденный тверской Онфилог: Why this is not the Tver Onfilog sought
strings.Акт относится к Рязанской земле. В нём н: The deed belongs to the Ryazan land. It contains no Nikolskoye Svechino, Khorvach volost, Yurlovs, or a move of the family to Tver uyezd. The name and the right generation match, but there is as yet no documentary geographical bridge.
strings.Разъезжая грамота оформлена как Record P: The boundary charter is set up as Record PUB-ASEI3-1483-RYAZAN-ANTIPA-ANFILOGOV. It shows separately the directly acting Antipa and his father Anfilog, reconstructed from his patronymic.
strings.носитель отдельного близкозвучного имени: bearer of a separate similar-sounding name in 16th-century deeds of the Kalyazin Monastery
strings.Назван в именном указателе к акту № 132: Named in the name index to deed No. 132 of «Актов Троицкого Калязина монастыря XVI в.» ["Acts of the Trinity Kalyazin Monastery, 16th century"]. This is a new person from the published Tver deed circle, but not a candidate for the founder of Onfilogovo: his name Onfim is independent and the document is not connected with the village sought.
strings.Онфим — личное имя; Негодяй — мирское пр: Onfim is the given name; Negodyai a secular nickname; Ushakov syn a patronymic or patronymic designation from Ushak. The three-part formula shows why the same person may appear in different indexes under his given name, his nickname or his father's name.
strings.Онфим и Онфилог — не одно имя: Onfim and Onfilog are not the same name
strings.Совпадение первых четырёх букв недостато: A match of the first four letters is not enough. Onfim is an independent Old Russian form of the name Anfim, whereas Onfilog/Anfilog belongs to a different name family, usually compared with Amfilokhy, Amfil and colloquial forms that became mixed with them. The final -log cannot be dropped without a document.
strings.Имя найдено именно в калязинском актовом: The name was found precisely in the 16th-century Kalyazin deed corpus connected with the Tver landholding world. It warns of the main trap of the search: OCR, cursive script or a brief index can confuse Onfim and Onfilog, so every similar match must be checked against the image and the full line.
strings.Деревня Онфимова как контроль: The village of Onfimova as a control
strings.На печатной с. 134 того же тома в межево: On printed p. 134 of the same volume a boundary formula names «царевы великого князя земля деревни Онфимова» ["the tsar and grand prince's land of the village of Onfimova"]. This is a literal example of another possessive toponym: Onfim-ov-a, a village associated with Onfim. It confirms the naming mechanism itself, but does not explain Onfilogovo.
strings.Ни акт № 132, ни деревня Онфимова не сод: Neither deed No. 132 nor the village of Onfimova contains Nikolskoye Svechino, Beloglazovo, the Yurlovs or the Onfilogovo sought. The find has therefore been added as a control of reading and of the meaning of the name, not as a new version of the founder's identity.
strings.бобыль деревни Колюбаево; поздний носите: bobyl of the village of Kolyubayevo; a late bearer of the stem Anfil-
strings.деревня Колюбаево на реке Верексе, Рожал: village of Kolyubayevo on the river Vereksa, Rozhalovsky stan of Uglich uyezd
strings.Прямо записан в 1629/1630 году в угличск: Recorded directly in 1629/1630 in the Uglich village of Kolyubayevo on the Vereksa. The name matters for the history of the form Anfil-, but the man lived almost ninety years after the first record of Onfilogovo and cannot be its founder.
strings.В статье 107 на печатной с. 412 читается: Entry 107 on printed p. 412 reads: «Дер. Колюбаево, на рчк. на Верекче, а в ней: во дв. б. Тимошка Анфилов» ["Village of Kolyubayevo, on the stream Verekcha, and in it: in a bobyl household Timoshka Anfilov"]. The reading has been checked against the page image.
strings.Тимошка — бытовая форма Тимофея. Анфилов: Timoshka is an everyday form of Timofei. Anfilov is a designation in -ov from the rare name Anfil; it may preserve the father's name, but the absence of the word «сын» ["son"] does not allow a biography of a separate older Anfil to be created unconditionally.
strings.Сокращение «во дв. б.» означает бобыльск: The abbreviation «во дв. б.» ["in a b. household"] means a bobyl household. Timoshka was a registered bobyl head of household, not the owner of a votchina; the land was held by Ivan Yuryevich Neledinsky.
strings.Колюбаево находилось на Верексе в Рожало: Kolyubayevo lay on the Vereksa in Rozhalovsky stan of Uglich uyezd. The exact site of the vanished village has not yet been found; the map marker shows the basin near the mouth of the Vereksa and is not presented as the coordinates of the household.
strings.Тимошка записан в 1629/1630 году, когда: Timoshka was recorded in 1629/1630, when the Tver name was already at least ninety years old. Both the date and the ownership complex rule him out as the eponym; the value of the find lies in the proven continuation of the name stem Anfil- in Uglich uyezd.
strings.Профиль P9655 и запись PUB-LIPINSKY-1629: Profile P9655 and Record PUB-LIPINSKY-1629-KOLYUBAEVO-TIMOSHKA-ANFILOV preserve the full transcription, status, source, map and directions for further research.
strings.Стефанида, жена Ивана Юрлова, держит сел: Stefanida, wife of Ivan Yurlov, holds the village (selo) of Nikolskoye Svechino with the church of St Nicholas the Wonderworker and six villages: Onfilogovo, Sadykovo, Ishkovo, Ostrogino, Voronino, Popovo. The literal line does not call her a widow; A. V. Matison characterises Ivan as a former owner who lived before 1539. In all, the holding comprises 18 households, 19 men and 206 chetverts of arable land per field.
strings.Название Онфилогово образовано от личног: The name Onfilogovo is formed from the personal name Onfilog: the stem Onfilog- and the possessive suffix -ov- give the meaning "Onfilog's settlement", "the place of Onfilog". Most probably the name is connected with the church name Amfilokhy (Amphilochius), but onomastic literature warns of possible confusion of similar forms from the names Amfil, Ampely and Amply. The bearer of the name may have been the founder, the first owner or another person with whom the settlement was firmly associated; a toponym alone does not allow the exact role to be established.
strings.Чего документ не доказывает: What the document does not prove
strings.Имена жителей четырёх дворов, имя владел: The names of the inhabitants of the four households, the name of the eponymous owner, his surname and the date of the village's foundation are not given in the book. This has been checked against the original on ll. 183v–184, not only against the abridged publication. The survey book of 1551–1554 does not reveal the predecessor either: Stefanida Yurlova did not present the scribes with any documents for the holding. This does not prove that no charters existed.
strings.Официальная цифровая опись РГАДА к д. 16: The official digital inventory of RGADA for d. 16081 opens, after entry No. 270, a section of vacant lands of Yuryevsky stan, not a continuation of Mikulinsky stan. Within this section the same ownership cluster that in 1539/1540 belonged to Stefanida Yurlova was found. Entry No. 272: «поместье Микиты Старкова, пустошь Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["the pomestye of Mikita Starkov, the waste land Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"]. Entry No. 276: pomestye of Veriga Bulbin, waste lands Nikolskoye also called Svechino, Sadykovo, Ishkovo. Entry No. 310: pomestye of Semyon Yurlov, waste lands Strechino, Voronino, Popovo, Miniforovo, Tyurchilovo, Belkovo, Portayevo. The coincidence of five settlements of the original cluster at once and of Yuryevsky stan rules out a random Anfilogovo of the same name. The inventory shows that after the Time of Troubles the former holding broke up among at least three holders, and the settlements turned into waste lands. Source: RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, part 2, d. 16081; official images 0126–0127: http://rgada.info/dela/1209/1/1209-opis_94i/0126.jpg and http://rgada.info/dela/1209/1/1209-opis_94i/0127.jpg.
strings.Микита — документальная форма имени Ники: Mikita is the documentary form of the name Nikita. The formula «поместье Микиты Старкова» ["the pomestye of Mikita Starkov"] names the holder of the land after 1634/1635, but not the former owner and not the eponym: Onfilogovo existed at least 95 years before this record and already bore the name of another person. Mikita's value is that he provides the first personal entry point found into the later history of precisely our waste land. The full text of d. 16081 may give his patronymic, the grounds for the grant, the previous holder and the boundaries.
strings.В статье № 272 второе название палеограф: In entry No. 272 the second name reads palaeographically as «Белоглазово тож» ["also called Beloglazovo"]. The existing village of Beloglazovo in Zubtsov okrug lies at 56.316667, 35.242500, on the left bank of the Rzhat, only 2.42 km from the scholarly reconstruction of Nikolskoye Svechino (56.322586, 35.204732) and about 4 km from Pervitino. The combination of a rare double name, the right stan and the neighbouring ownership cluster allows the later Beloglazovo to be identified with high confidence with the former Anfilogovo. The marker is moved to Beloglazovo as the most precise modern location; the position of the 16th-century households within the settlement remains approximate.
strings.Формула XVII века «Анфилогово, Белоглазо: The 17th-century formula «Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"] opens two different historical possibilities. The first: these are two successive layers of the name, the old Onfilogovo and a later Beloglazovo derived from another person or family designation. The second: a single eponym may have been known by the church-everyday name Onfilog and the secular nickname Beloglaz, so the settlement preserved both sides of one naming. The nickname Beloglaz itself is real for the period: S. B. Veselovsky's Onomastikon names Prince Ivan Ivanovich Lykov Beloglaz in the first half of the 16th century and derives the Beloglazov-Lykovs from him. Archival rules and onomastic studies confirm that the construction «тож» ["also called"] could join an official and a popular name, or an old and a new one. But the exact combination «Онфилог Белоглаз» ["Onfilog Beloglaz"] has not been found in the indexes examined or in full-text search. Therefore the two names cannot be merged into the biography of a single person without an early charter, boundary description or witness formula. Sources: Onomastikon — https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/Spravochniki/onomastikon-drevnerusskie-imena-prozvishha-i-familii/ ; rules for describing double names — https://www.consultant.ru/document/cons_doc_LAW_437738/8c4f4dac2a91c1941b2e6a0e504d51daeb67382d/ .
strings.Полностью проверен 867-страничный скан Н: The 867-page scan of N. M. Tupikov's Slovar drevnerusskikh lichnykh sobstvennykh imen (Dictionary of Old Russian Personal Proper Names; St Petersburg, 1903) has been fully checked: all pages were OCR-processed, a search was run for the forms Onfilog, Onpilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Amfilog, Amfilokh, Anfilof, Onfilof, Ampilog and Ampelog, and relevant passages were verified against the images. The dictionary yielded not a single new bearer of the stem sought. This negative result must not be turned into proof of an extremely rare or unique use of the name: the dictionary is devoted primarily to non-calendar names, whereas Onfilog most probably goes back to the Christian Amfilokhy (Amphilochius). Nevertheless, the check closes off one more large compendium of references to scribal books and published deeds of the 15th–17th centuries. Digital copy: https://rusneb.ru/catalog/000199_000009_003717568/ .
strings.На с. 497 словаря Тупикова найдены две п: On p. 497 of Tupikov's dictionary two verified parallels to the second name of the village were found. «Куземко Белоглазов» ["Kuzemko Beloglazov"] is a Smolensk peasant of 1609; «князь Семён Семёнов сын Белоглазова Лыкова» ["Prince Semyon, son of Semyon Beloglazov-Lykov"] is a Moscow nobleman of 1598. They show that at the end of the 16th and beginning of the 17th century Beloglazov could be both a peasant family designation and a princely clan sobriquet. This strengthens the version of Beloglazov as a separate, later eponym, but neither of the two men is connected with Tver uyezd, Mikita Starkov or our settlement. Tupikov's sources: Akty istoricheskie [Historical Acts]. Vol. II. P. 247; Akty Moskovskogo gosudarstva [Acts of the Muscovite State]. Vol. II. P. 44; consolidated publication: N. M. Tupikov. Slovar drevnerusskikh lichnykh sobstvennykh imyon [Dictionary of Old Russian Personal Proper Names]. St Petersburg, 1903. P. 497.
strings.Второе название владельческого центра —: The second name of the estate centre, Svechino, may preserve not only an everyday designation but also the name of a service family. A secondary genealogical compilation derives the Svechins from the Tver boyar circle: Andrei Konstantinovich, nicknamed Svecha, is named as the founder of the line around the middle of the 15th century; his sons Fyodor and Karp belong roughly to the generation of the 1470s; his grandson Matvei Fyodorovich was a Novy Torzhok landholder recorded in the Dvorovaya tetrad [Court Register] of the 1550s. Pyotr Matveyevich Svechin, a Novy Torzhok pomestye holder, is documented in the Tver service list of 1585 and in 1580 took part in the description of Simeon Bekbulatovich's possessions in Tver uyezd. This establishes a real Tver–Novy Torzhok line of the surname of the right period and a new address for searching the ownership charters of Nikolskoye Svechino. However, no text found so far states directly that this particular family owned our village or gave it its name; the similarity Svechino – Svechin remains a testable ownership hypothesis. Sources: genealogical compilation — https://rod-i-predki.ru/sample-page/materinskaya-liniya/xviii/218-2 ; Tver list of 1585 — https://vostlit.info/Texts/Dokumenty/Russ/XVI/1560-1580/Akty_Popov_I/21-40/30.htm ; Tysyachnaya kniga [Book of the Thousand] and Dvorovaya tetrad — https://yakovkrotov.com/acts/16/2/tysyachnaya_10.htm .
strings.Возможное объяснение фразы 1551—1554 год: A possible explanation of the 1551–1554 phrase «писма не давала» ["she did not present a document"] is connected with the Tver fire of 1537. The Cathedral of the Transfiguration of the Saviour served as a repository not only of church but also of private acts, and in the great fire documents perished together with it. Studies of the scribal books note that landholders of the mid-16th century did indeed refer to the loss of charters in fires, especially the Moscow fire of 1547 and the Tver fire of 1537. Therefore the charters of Ivan and Stefanida Yurlov may have perished before the survey. But the entry on Stefanida does not mention a fire and does not explain why no document was presented: the version is probable in the local context, not directly established for her archive. Overview of the storage and loss of acts — https://history.wikireading.ru/395765 ; context of the scribal books and fire losses — https://history.wikireading.ru/232103 ; official archival passport of the complex — https://unikdoc.rusarchives.ru/0406-2010-piscovye-i-dozornye-knigi-tverskogo-uezda-serediny-16-veka .
strings.Три статьи показывают не смену одного вл: The three entries show not the replacement of one owner by another but the fragmentation of the complex. Mikita Starkov ended up with Anfilogovo/Beloglazovo; Veriga Bulbin with the centre Nikolskoye Svechino and the villages Sadykovo and Ishkovo; Semyon Yurlov with Voronino and Popovo together with other waste lands. Ostrogino has not yet been found in the fragment examined. Semyon Yurlov is important as a later bearer of the same family designation, but his kinship with Ivan and Stefanida has not been established; the study by A. V. Kazakov specifically warns that Ivan Timofeyevich Yurlov the Elder left no male descendants in Lithuania.
strings.Справочник А. В. Матисона выявляет в Тве: A. V. Matison's reference book reveals a large circle of Starkovs in Tver uyezd already by 1551: Vasily and Ivan Semyonovich, Grigory, Grigory Matveyevich, Grigory Semyonovich, Yelizar Vasilyevich, Ivan Grigoryevich, Kolmak Ivanovich, Kropot Yepifanovich, Semyon Matveyevich and Fyodor Ivanovich. Their known lands lay in Volkovo, Krenkovo and Neyelovo; Nikolskoye Svechino, Onfilogovo and Beloglazovo are not named in these entries. A separate neighbouring village, Tetyulkino, already in a deed of gift of 1550/1551 had the second name Starkovo, but it was transferred by Tit Dmitriyev son of Aleksandrov to Ulyana, widow of Fyodor Davydov, and to her son Veriga — without any Starkov being named. Therefore Mikita Starkov's surname and the toponym Starkovo show a local Starkov trace, but so far yield neither Mikita's pedigree nor the passage of Anfilogovo from Stefanida. Sources: A. V. Matison. Dvoryanstvo Tverskogo uezda XVI — nachala XVIII vekov [The Nobility of Tver Uyezd, 16th – early 18th Centuries]. Moscow, 2023. Pp. 251–252; PM-XVI. Pp. 246–247; Akty sluzhilykh zemlevladeltsev XV — nachala XVII veka [Acts of Service Landholders, 15th – early 17th Century]. Vol. I. Moscow, 1997. No. 82, p. 65.
strings.Полнотекстово проверены оба первых тома: Both first volumes of «Акты служилых землевладельцев XV — начала XVII века» ["Acts of Service Landholders, 15th – early 17th Century"] were checked in full text: volume I (1997) for all variants Onfilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Ampilog, Amfilog, Anfilof and the short stems; volume II (1998) through its complete digital text. No new bearers of the rare name, nor Nikolskoye Svechino, our Anfilogovo/Beloglazovo or Yurlov were found in these two volumes. In addition, the index of about 3,700 descriptions of private acts of the 15th – early 17th century published by A. V. Antonov was checked: the list of persons contains no stems Anfil-, Yurlov-, Svechin- or Starkov-. The edition confirmed only the neighbouring acts on Mikitino and Tetyulkino/Starkovo involving Veriga Fyodorovich Davydov. This narrows the search within the published private archives: the decisive document is more likely hidden in the Tver scribal and transfer books, in the lost estate archive of the Yurlovs or in monastic copy books, rather than in the first two volumes of the ASZ. Electronic publication of the index to Antonov's reference book: https://62info.ru/history/node/11442 .
strings.В «Тверских актах», вып. 1, акт № XIV, с: In «Тверские акты» ["Tver Acts"], issue 1, act No. XIV, pp. 60–61, a deed of gift of 7076 (1567/1568) was found from Stepan Yakovlevich Oskolkov to the Osipov Monastery for the votchina village of Ostrogino in Tver uyezd, Yuryevsky stan. Oskolkov states literally that he bought it from the brothers Ivan and Matvei, sons of Timofei Tsyzyrev, for 32 roubles. This yields an ownership sequence: Ivan and Matvei Timofeyevich Tsyzyrev → Stepan Yakovlevich Oskolkov → Osipov Monastery. It could explain the absence of Ostrogino from the late secular inventory of Stefanida's disintegrated complex, but for now it is only a testable parallel.
strings.Первичные страницы 191 и 234 дозора 1551: Primary pages 191 and 234 of the 1551–1554 survey were checked against the scans. The Tsyzyrev brothers appear as owners of Ostrogino only after the formula «а нынеча» ["and now"]; the secondary date of 1540 was an error. Their village had 15 chetverts of arable land and 10 kopnas of hay and is printed under the heading of the volosts of the Mikulin appanage. Stefanida's Ostrogino in 1539/1540 had 19 chetverts and 20 kopnas and belonged to the complex of Nikolskoye Svechino in Khorvach. The different sizes and headings make a separate settlement of the same name or a separate share more probable than full identity. At the same time, the editor of the 1567/1568 act referred directly to p. 191, while the act itself places the Tsyzyrevs' Ostrogino in Yuryevsky stan. The administrative discrepancy has not yet been explained; the chain is not included in the history of Onfilogovo as a proven fact.
strings.На с. 234 того же дозора отец братьев ус: On p. 234 of the same survey the brothers' father is established literally: «Тимофея Семенова сына Цузырева» ["of Timofei, son of Semyon Tsuzyrev"]; further it is said «Тимофея в животе не стало» ["Timofei is no longer alive"], and the present holders of Sholygino on the stream Zhidokhov are named as «дети его Матюшка да Иван» ["his children Matyushka and Ivan"]. A deed of purchase is noted for Matvei. The family documentedly lived in Khorvach volost, Yuryevsky stan, but neither Nikolskoye Svechino nor Onfilogovo is named in its entry. Matvei's deed of purchase becomes a new documentary address for searching for boundary neighbours, not proof of ownership of Stefanida's village.
strings.Официальная цифровая опись РГАДА по Твер: The official digital inventory of RGADA for Tver uyezd, section 94, frame 0123, entry No. 197, literally contains «Анфилов починок» ["Anfilov new clearing"] within a long list of the pomestye of Prince Aleksandr Gorbaty. An enlarged image confirms these two words but does not confirm the earlier reading «село Перевитино» ["the village of Perevitino"]: it has been withdrawn as too bold a decipherment of a cramped cursive line. Archival address: RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, part 2, d. 16081, ll. 1–407. The section heading assigns the entry to Mikulinsky stan, whereas Nikolskoye Svechino and our Onfilogovo lay in Khorvach volost. Not a single stable neighbour of Stefanida's complex — Sadykovo, Ishkovo, Ostrogino, Voronino or Popovo — has been confidently established in the brief inventory. Therefore this is an independent Tver toponym from the name Anfil, and not a found early name of our Onfilogovo. Image of the inventory: http://rgada.info/dela/1209/1/1209-opis_94i/0123.jpg.
strings.В официальной описи д. 16057 заголовок В: In the official inventory of d. 16057 the heading of Volovitsky stan was found on frame 0089; the section begins with entry No. 121 and continues approximately until the transition to the next stan on frame 0100. Machine and manual examination of the available owners' index revealed no stable cluster Nikolskoye (Svechino) – Onfilogovo – Voronino – Sadykovo. This is a limited negative result for the index, not for the full text of d. 16057 nor for the separate copy d. 872.
strings.Нужен полный текст статьи № 197 о помест: The full text of entry No. 197 on the pomestye of Prince Aleksandr Gorbaty is needed: only it will make it possible to read the neighbouring settlements, boundaries and the possible history of the Anfilov new clearing. The printed extract of 1916 promised to include Mikulinsky, Khorvatsky and Yuryevsky stans in the second issue, so this entry could potentially have been published there; however, the available digital issues of the journal for 1915 do not contain the supplement. For our settlement the main item remains the full text of entry No. 272 of d. 16081 — «Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"] — and not entry No. 197.
strings.Первичные сканы московских исповедных ве: Primary scans of Moscow confession registers document a late Uglich–Yukhot cluster. In 1851 Yefim Anfilogov, aged 17, is named as a peasant's son of Count Sheremetev from Uglich uyezd: Central State Archive of Moscow (TsGA Moskvy), f. 2122, op. 1, d. 864, scan 55, https://yandex.ru/archive/catalog/ea71c6ce-dcaf-4363-a449-d6c4a90e1705/55 . In 1853 Deomid Anfilogov, aged 23, is named as a peasant of Count Sheremetev from the village of Kostyurina, and Yevgraf Anfilogov, aged 19, as a peasant's son from «деревни юхотской» ["a Yukhot village"]: TsGA Moskvy, f. 203, op. 747, d. 1647, scan 206, https://yandex.ru/archive/catalog/7ecf2e7a-e7e1-4383-9658-92858f953b9a/206 . A parallel copy of 1853 is in f. 2122, op. 1, d. 864, scans 101–102. The kinship of the three men with each other and with Tonkoi Onfilogov has not been established.
strings.На скане метрической книги за 1859 год Д: On the scan of the 1859 parish register Dmitry is recorded as «Димитрій Анфилогѣевъ» ["Dimitry Anfilogeyev"], and again as «Анфилогиевъ» ["Anfilogiyev"], not literally Anfilogov. Yevgraf's new chain shows that the forms Anfilogov, Anfilogiyev and Amfilokhiyev could refer to one person and render a patronymic from Amfilokhy. Therefore Dmitry can no longer simply be excluded from the Kostyurino cluster: his literal form is kept separately, and kinship with the Strunkins remains unverified. Source: TsGA Moskvy, f. 2122, op. 1, d. 863, scan 131, https://yandex.ru/archive/catalog/f50452c0-a34b-485d-8caf-98525e7169b4/131 .
strings.Ведомость 1858 года называет 25-летнего: The register of 1858 names a 25-year-old Kostyurino peasant «Ефграф Анфилогиев» ["Yefgraf Anfilogiyev"]; by age, owner, uyezd and parish this is the same 19-year-old Yefgraf Anfilogov of 1853. Two parish register entries of 1858 and 1864 reveal his full name: Yevgraf Amfilokhiyev Strunkin. In the same entries the children's father is Diomid Amfilokhiyev Strunkin; in the confession register he is recorded as Deomid Anfilogeyev. The combination of independent forms proves a real father named Amfilokhy Strunkin, who lived at the end of the 18th – beginning of the 19th century. Sources: TsGA Moskvy, f. 2122, op. 1, d. 864, scan 198, https://yandex.ru/archive/catalog/ea71c6ce-dcaf-4363-a449-d6c4a90e1705/198 ; f. 2123, op. 1, d. 211, scans 204 and 227, https://yandex.ru/archive/catalog/c236ed4e-4d82-42b4-9d1a-338949440456/204 and https://yandex.ru/archive/catalog/c236ed4e-4d82-42b4-9d1a-338949440456/227 .
strings.Прежний поиск смерти Деомида за 1853–185: The earlier search for Deomid's death in 1853–1858 relied on an erroneous marital link. Negative search results do not prove a date of death; the time frame has been withdrawn.
strings.Опубликованная исследовательская выпись: A published research extract from the parish register of the Church of St Clement in Yukhot for 1850 names a godmother from Kostyurino: «крестьянская девка Александра Амфиногиева» ["the peasant maiden Aleksandra Amfinogiyeva"] — GAYaO, f. 230, op. 2, d. 1004, l. 557 verso. In the language of parish registers such a form is usually a patronymic: Aleksandra, daughter of Amfinogy/Amfilokhy. Without an image of the original and the neighbouring family in the confession register she cannot automatically be considered a sister of the Strunkins, but this is an independent sign of the presence of the same personal name in Kostyurino. Publication: https://forum.yar-genealogy.ru/index.php?showtopic=11879 .
strings.Официальный каталог ГАЯО подтверждает оц: The official catalogue of GAYaO confirms the digitised file: f. 100, op. 7, d. 250, «Ревизские сказки крестьян разных вотчин Ярославского уезда за 1782 год» ["Revision tales of peasants of various votchinas of Yaroslavl uyezd for 1782"], 1,401 leaves, https://af.yar-archives.ru/archive1/unit/10000357031 . A research index by settlement places Kostyurino on l. 476. The portal provides the images only after authorisation through ESIA and arranging remote access; without such viewing the names of the inhabitants in 1782 are not considered verified. This leaf is the closest direct path to the generation of the father, Amfilokhy Strunkin.
strings.Каталог Центра архивных документов в Угл: The catalogue of the Centre for Archival Documents in Uglich contains a separate file «Деревня Костюрино» ["The village of Kostyurino"]: f. R-850, op. 1, d. 4361, https://af.yar-archives.ru/archive5/unit/10000304662 . Fond R-850 is titled «Межевые планы Угличского уезда» ["Survey plans of Uglich uyezd"], so the outside dates 1750–1936 refer to the range of the entire cartographic complex and do not mean that the file holds a family chronicle for every year. The file has not been digitised. Its value lies in the exact boundary and neighbours of Kostyurino; the catalogue does not mention the names Amfilokhy or the Strunkins.
strings.Поиск по официальному каталогу выявил дв: A search of the official catalogue revealed two early files relating directly to the village. Centre for Archival Documents in Uglich, f. 59, op. 1, d. 220: in 1786 a serf of Count Sheremetev, Andrei Vasilyev, from the village of Kostyurino in Yukhot volost is named; https://af.yar-archives.ru/archive5/unit/10000164739 . GAYaO, f. 150, op. 1, vol. 1, d. 667: a file of 1803 on the ploughing over of the boundary between the economic village of Zhukovo and the peasant village of Kostyurino belonging to Count Sheremetev; https://af.yar-archives.ru/archive1/unit/10000897393 . Neither file has yet been digitised. They confirm the continuous belonging of Kostyurino to the Sheremetev complex and may name the village circle of adult men of Amfilokhy's generation, but Amfilokhy himself is not mentioned in the titles.
strings.В библиотечном указателе Ярославского ис: In the library index of the Yaroslavl Historical and Genealogical Society a description was found of competition work No. 32 «Судьба отходника» ["The Fate of a Seasonal Migrant Worker"], 2009, author I. Klyukin. The main family of the work is the peasant Korytovs of the village of Borok; among the related surnames «Стрункин (крестьяне, с. Костюрино)» ["Strunkin (peasants, village of Kostyurino)"] is listed separately, and the appendix contained photographs and photocopies of documents. Publication: https://forum.yar-genealogy.ru/index.php?showtopic=6623 , post No. 4. The YarIRO library page states that anyone may request to view the materials: https://www.yar-genealogy.ru/0220.php . The work itself has not been found online; for now unknown names or kinship links cannot be taken over from it. This is potentially the fastest non-archival path to an already compiled Strunkin branch.
strings.Официальный каталог РГИА подтверждает: ф: The official catalogue of RGIA confirms: f. 1088, op. 7, d. 16 — an extract from the scribal, survey and census books of the Yukhot votchina for 1629–1631, 1676–1679 and 1706, with an end date of 21 July 1707, https://fgurgia.ru/object/205714361 ; f. 1088, op. 7, d. 65 — a copy from the census books for the Yukhot votchina, https://fgurgia.ru/object/205772177 . A research description dates d. 65 to 1754 and mentions family-by-family lists with ages. In both cases the correct fond is 1088; the number 188 that has been encountered is an error. The catalogue shows no open digital copies, so the files remain addresses for future archival viewing, not evidence already read.
strings.Историческая Костюрина — современное Кос: Historical Kostyurina is modern Kostyurino on the left bank of the Yukhot, 57.750225, 38.520101. The economic description of 1798 counts 11 households, 36 males and 38 females: RGIA, f. 1350, op. 312, d. 197. To Tonkoi Onfilogov's Priluki it is about 52 km in a straight line. However, Kostyurina belonged to the Sheremetevs' Yukhot votchina, whereas Priluki was an ancient possession of the Trinity-St Sergius Monastery. Consequently, this is a regional proximity of the rare name, not a proven single ownership or kinship complex.
strings.Нечёткий полнотекстовый поиск по OCR все: Fuzzy full-text search over the OCR of the entire volume, Levenshtein distance ≤ 2 from the normalised forms of the surname.
strings.Проверены полнотекстовая публикация 1877: The following were checked: the full-text publication of 1877, a digital image of the original RGADA book, the early section of the 1896 edition «Тверские акты» ["Tver Acts"], the available full-text volumes of «Акты служилых землевладельцев» ["Acts of Service Landholders"], all 349 open pages of A. V. Matison's 2023 reference book and all digitised regular issues of «Тверские епархиальные ведомости» ["Tver Diocesan Gazette"] for 1915. No direct document naming the Tver Onfilog has been found so far. Matison, however, confirmed the former owner of the complex as «Юрлов Иван (до 1539)» ["Yurlov Ivan (before 1539)"] and linked him with Nikolskoye Svechino held by his wife Stefanida. For 1627–1628 a narrow address has been established: a separate copy of the scribal book of Volovitsky stan by the scribe Fyodor Ignatyev — RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, part 1, d. 872, ll. 1–191; the general copy of the same census — f. 1209, op. 1, part 2, d. 16057, ll. 1–701, with an index of owners on ll. 1–28. An additional later list of lands of Mikulinsky, Yuryevsky and Voskresensky stans after 7143 — d. 16081, ll. 1–407. D. 875, earlier mistakenly called its copy, is in fact an independent copy of another scribal book by Fyodor Ignatyev of 1627–1628; it must not be substituted for d. 16081. For the next generation the census of 1677/1678, d. 16060, is needed, and the 1710 complex: the general copy d. 16083, while Volovitsky stan proper, according to Matison's reference book, lies at the junction of dd. 16086–16087. The online publication contains only selected fragments, so the absence of Onfilogovo in it is not a negative result.
strings.Каталог писцовых и переписных книг Тверс: Catalogue of the scribal and census books of Tver uyezd with a separate copy for Volovitsky stan: https://dompredkov.ru/tverskie-pistsovye-i-perepisnye-knigi/ ; reference guide to the 1710 censuses with the beginning of Volovitsky stan on l. 178: https://census1710.narod.ru/spravka/spisok1710.htm ; a selective, not complete, publication of fragments of dd. 16083–16084: https://genealogia.ru/1710/1710-god-perepisnaya-kniga-tverskogo-uezd
strings.В архивной копии научной ГИС «Тверской у: In an archived copy of the academic GIS «Тверской уезд в XVI веке» ["Tver Uyezd in the 16th Century"], object No. 2188 «Николское Свечино» ["Nikolskoye Svechino"] is located at the point 56.3225861843296, 35.2047323324939 and attributed to Stefanida, wife of Ivan Yurlov; the 1551–1554 layer repeats the same point. The dependent villages of the estate, including Onfilogovo, are not plotted as separate objects. The checked layer of 95 published private acts does not contain Nikolskoye Svechino, Onfilogovo or the Yurlovs; the nearest, Roslovl with Mikhail Beleutov, is a different estate.
strings.Слой 1539/1540 года: https://web.archive: Layer for 1539/1540: https://web.archive.org/web/20230807031437id_/http://tver.histgeo.ru/layers/1539_8.js ; layer for 1551–1554: https://web.archive.org/web/20230807062104id_/http://tver.histgeo.ru/layers/1551_7.js ; layer of published charters: https://web.archive.org/web/20180522140917id_/http://tver.histgeo.ru/layers/Charterslabeled_1.js
strings.На современной карте в 626 метрах к запа: On the modern map, 626 metres west of the academic point of object No. 2188, lies the village of Nikolskoye (approximately 56.32047, 35.19532; OKTMO 28653464171). This is a strong additional indication of the area of historical Nikolskoye Svechino, but not proof of identity: in the 1859 sequence of populated places along the river Gzhat no separate Nikolskoye was found, whereas Pervitino, Belavino, Yagodina, Shepelevo, Beloglazovo and Yuryevskaya are recorded. The PGM now confirms that the village of Onfilogova itself lay separately from Nikolskoye and directly next to the village of Voronina. Until the sheet is georeferenced, the marker is left on the academic reconstruction of the estate centre and retains approximate precision.
strings.Проверены все 18 открытых листов плана Г: All 18 open sheets of the General Land Survey plan of Zubtsov uyezd were checked. On sheet 1–3 the neighbouring «д. Воронина» ["village of Voronina"] and «д. Онфилогова» ["village of Onfilogova"] are legibly labelled; the label of Onfilogova is within survey plot No. 516. The coincidence of the pair is especially conclusive because both villages belong to one possession of Stefanida in the scribal book of 1539/1540. The PGM establishes that Onfilogova survived until the era of the General Land Survey and separates it from the estate centre of Nikolskoye Svechino. Source: https://poisk.yapl.ru/show-pgm.php?id_map=23-155-1-3.jpg ; table of contents of the set: https://poisk.yapl.ru/pgm-uezd.php?way=23-155 . The next targeted document is the economic notes of Zubtsov uyezd for plot No. 516.
strings.Найден и полностью просмотрен отдельный: A separate manuscript alphabetical index to the fifth census revision of Zubtsov uyezd was found and examined in full: GATO, f. 312, op. 4, d. 14497, 1794–1808; FamilySearch, film 2201895, DGS 005371275, part 15, frames 775–819. The index is arranged by owners: within each estate the dependent settlements and the number of revision souls are listed, and later annotations record movements of the population. The letter «О» ["O"] on frame 797 denotes owners' surnames, not a geographical section. A continuous check of all leaves for the stable pair «Онфилогова» ["Onfilogova"] and «Воронина» ["Voronina"] produced no match. This does not prove that the village disappeared: the index records population, so a separate land village without revision souls may not have been included. On frame 800 the neighbouring large Pervitino estate is confidently recognised: the village of Pervitino and the villages of Selivanovo, Raslovo, Sablino, Osipovo, Rodionkovo, Nikolskoye, Yagodino, Belavino, Vasilyevskoye, Golovino, Bukino, Romashkovo, Bykovo and Plyusninskoye. This composition coincides with the later list of the parish of the Kazan Church of Pervitino. According to the 1782 census revision Pervitino belonged to the heirs of Pyotr Semyonovich Khlopov, but Onfilogova and Voronina are not among his settlements; therefore proximity on the map gives no right to attribute plot No. 516 to the Khlopovs.
strings.В исторической описи тверских «дел стары: In the historical inventory of the Tver «дел старых лет» ["files of old years"], file No. 21 of 1702 was found: «Дело Михаила Федорова сына Пушкина и Родиона Пунина сына Юрлова о розыске межи их межевых поместий или межевых земель, состоящих в Тверском уезде» ["File of Mikhail, son of Fyodor Pushkin, and Rodion, son of Punya Yurlov, on the investigation of the boundary of their surveyed pomestyes or surveyed lands situated in Tver uyezd"] (the middle of the formula is read with slight palaeographic uncertainty; the general sense of a boundary dispute is clear). Begun on 21 January 1702, decided on 7 February of the same year, 6 leaves. Archival reference: RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, part 2, d. 16089, register entry No. 21; image of page 47 of the inventory: http://rgada.info/dela/1209/1/1209-opis_948i/0045.jpg . The name «Родион Пунин сын Юрлов» ["Rodion, son of Punya, Yurlov"] means Rodion, son of Punya, of the Yurlov designation; the word «Пунин» ["Punin"] here is a patronymic form, not a second modern surname. This is the first later Yurlov found in the current search who is directly connected with land in Tver uyezd. He has not been identified with Stefanida's husband and has not been proven to be a descendant of the same family: about 162 years separate the records. The main value of the find is a precise six-leaf document in which estates, neighbouring settlements, former owners and survey documents may be named.
strings.Полностью получены и машинно просмотрены: All 109 images of the owners' alphabetical index to the Tver files of old years, RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, dd. 16088–16122 (digital inventory 1137), were obtained in full and machine-examined, followed by 433 images of the detailed register of dd. 16088–16101 for 1700–1715 (digital inventory 948). Automatic matches were checked manually. The forms «Анфилогова» ["Anfilogova"] in the list of pomestyes of Perm uyezd and similar names in other uyezds were rejected as geographically unrelated; they cannot be transferred to the Tver village. The surname Yurlov was not found in the owners' index, but the detailed register revealed Rodion, son of Punya Yurlov, in d. 16089. This shows the limitation of the index: the absence of a surname in it does not replace an entry-by-entry examination of the files.
strings.РГАДА, ф. 1209, оп. 1, ч. 2, д. 16065, р: RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, part 2, d. 16065, register entry No. 161 of 9 November 7176 (1667/1668), is no longer considered a trace of our settlement. On the enlarged official image 0084 the double name reads «Анфилогово, Чагримово тож» ["Anfilogovo, also called Chagrimovo"], and not as the earlier erroneous variants «Филогово» ["Filogovo"] or «Дылово» ["Dylovo"]. Exactly this double name is already attested in 1588 for a separate village in the possession of Stepan Afanasyevich Likharev. Our place has a different stable second name — Beloglazovo — and a different ownership cluster: Nikolskoye Svechino, Sadykovo, Ishkovo, Ostrogino, Voronino and Popovo. Consequently, the four leaves of entry No. 161 may be useful for the history of the namesake, but are not a priority in the search for the Tver eponym of Onfilogovo/Beloglazovo. Official image: http://rgada.info/dela/1209/1/1209-opis_227i/0084.jpg .
strings.В интерактивной базе «Дом предков» прове: In the interactive database «Дом предков» ["House of Ancestors"], 421,095 entries on service people of the 17th–18th centuries were checked. The surname stem Yurlov yielded 118 entries, but the filter combination Yurlov + Tver yielded zero. Among the rare forms, the following were found: «Онфилогов Фолимон» ["Onfilogov Folimon"], Oryol, 1689, document 210-5-68; four matches for Anfilog, including Fyodor Anfilogov, Oryol, 1642, document 210-4-260; 164 matches for Anpilog; zero for Ampilog and Filog. These results confirm the real use of the forms Onfilog-/Anfilog-/Anpilog- and the transition of a personal designation into a surname, but they do not name the Tver eponym: the bearers found are later than 1539/1540 and belong mainly to Oryol and Kromy. The absence of Tver matches is a limited negative result within the database, not proof that the family is absent from the sources.
strings.База служилых людей: https://next-fast-t: Database of service people: https://next-fast-table-gold.vercel.app/ ; description of its contents and list of the Tver sets: https://dompredkov.ru/spiski-sluzhilyh-lyudej-xvii-xviii-vekov/
strings.Полностью проверена 32-страничная опись: The 32-page inventory of collection 156 «Юрловы» ["The Yurlovs"] of the Archive of the St Petersburg Institute of History of the Russian Academy of Sciences (SPbII RAN) was checked in full. The collection relates mainly to the Kurmysh–Nizhny Novgorod branch and contains documents from 1670 onward; the forms Onfilogovo, Svechino, Anfilog and Filog are absent from the inventory. The only mention of Tver lands concerns the estates of the Chirikovs and the Zherebtsovs, not of the Yurlovs. Therefore this collection cannot be used as a genealogy of Stefanida and Ivan Yurlov; the negative result separates off a different branch of the family and narrows further searching to Tver scribal, transfer and land-survey files.
strings.Архив СПбИИ РАН, колл. 156 «Юрловы», опи: Archive of the SPbII RAN, coll. 156 «Юрловы» ["The Yurlovs"], inventory: https://spbiiran.ru/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/koll.-156.-yurlovy.pdf
strings.Самый близкий по времени персональный ка: The personal candidate closest in time was found in a copy book of the Trinity-Sergius Monastery for 1536/1537. The exact text of the publication: «Село Прилук на реке на Волге» ["The village of Priluk on the river Volga"], then, after the ploughing peasants, «а непашенных дворов: ... в. Тонкой Онфилогов» ["and of non-ploughing households: ... in the household Tonkoi Onfilogov"]. The abbreviation «в.» is expanded as «во дворе» ["in the household"]. Tonkoi was a monastery peasant recorded in a separate non-ploughing household, not a landholder; the total of the entry counts 21 non-ploughing households and 21 persons recorded in them across the whole Priluk complex. For naming in the first half of the 16th century, the form «Онфилогов» ["Onfilogov"] is possessive-patronymic: Tonkoi is Onfilog's man, above all his son. The source thereby independently attests a real man named Onfilog who lived one generation earlier and fits chronologically with the emergence of the name of the Tver village. The modern reconstructed points of Priluk and Nikolskoye Svechino are about 207.6 km apart in a straight line. Without a document on the migration, service or land of this family in Tver uyezd, the coincidence of name and time remains a strong hypothesis, but not an identification. Publication: S. M. Kashtanov, "On the Trail of the Trinity Copy Books of the 16th Century" (Po sledam troitskikh kopiynykh knig XVI v.) // Zapiski otdela rukopisey [Notes of the Manuscripts Department]. Issue 40. Moscow, 1979. P. 43; manuscript: GPB, Pogodin collection, No. 1846, l. 65 v.; PDF: https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/assets/uploads/zor/%D0%97%D0%9E%D0%A0_40.pdf .
strings.Найден прямой документальный маршрут общ: A direct documentary route of Tonkoi's community through the Tver land has been found. Act No. 294, dated 1461–1466, a grant charter of Grand Prince Mikhail Borisovich of Tver to the Trinity-Sergius Monastery, permitted duty-free passage through the Tver principality for the Trinity boats, fishermen and peasants of the Prisetsk and Priluk holdings to the river Sheksna. Act No. 303 of the same complex ordered the Kashin toll collectors to let two Trinity boats pass to the village of Priluk and back with grain; acts Nos. 295–297 confirm a steady movement of monastery people and goods through the Tver principality. An earlier charter, No. 265, of 1455–1462, required the return of peasants who had left the monastery villages of Uglich uyezd and forbade releasing those living there, that is, it records real mobility of the dependent population. This does not prove that the elder Onfilog or Tonkoi travelled specifically to Nikolskoye Svechino, but for the first time it replaces an abstract possibility of movement with a concrete historical corridor that their Priluk community used in the generation of the presumed father. Source: Akty sotsialno-ekonomicheskoy istorii Severo-Vostochnoy Rusi kontsa XIV – nachala XVI v. [Acts of the Socio-Economic History of North-Eastern Rus' of the Late 14th – Early 16th Century]. Vol. 1. Moscow, 1952, Nos. 265, 294–297, 303; electronic table of contents and regesta: https://www.vostlit.info/Texts/Dokumenty/Russ/XIV/1380-1400/Akty_Troic_Serg_mon/index.htm .
strings.Прилук был не изолированной земледельчес: Priluk was not an isolated farming village but an old Trinity economic and fishing complex on the left bank of the Volga, at the Kashin–Uglich boundary. The Uda holding of the Trinity-Sergius Monastery is documented as early as 1411, and privileges for Priluk by charters of the mid-15th century. The charters separately name the Priluk fishermen, Volga fishing grounds, boats, grain transport and duty-free passage through the Tver principality. Therefore Tonkoi's non-ploughing household may have been connected with fishing, river transport, trade or service to the monastery economy; the source does not state his exact occupation. Priluk's long ownership by the monastery weakens the simple version that Tonkoi or his father came there together with recent Yurlov land: there is no documented transfer between the ownership complexes. Context: M. S. Cherkasova, Krupnaya feodalnaya votchina v Rossii kontsa XVI–XVII veka [A Large Feudal Votchina in Russia of the Late 16th–17th Century]; acts Nos. 155, 294–297, 303; A. G. Bobrov, study of the early charters of the Trinity-Sergius Monastery: https://www.booksite.ru/civk/data/bobrov.pdf .
strings.Проверены два ближайших к поколению пред: The two early Priluk acts closest to the generation of the presumed elder Onfilog were checked. In a boundary-division charter of about 1495–1497, ASEI I, No. 581, the persons named are Ozarok Tregub, his brother Gavrilko, Kharko, the children of Grida, the Priluk elder Nikon, the peasant Klyapik with his companions, and the court officials; the forms Onfilog/Anfilog, Lodygin and Yurlov are absent. The full personal tail of the next document, of 1505/1506, No. 660, was reconstructed from overlapping search snippets of another digital copy on Google Books and checked against the name indexes of the volume. The boundary-division charter of Dmitry Kozhukhov between the land of Priluk and the lands of Nikolskoye-Ulemenskoye, the Drachkovo new clearing and other places near the Kashin boundary names five Priluk peasants — Mikifor the sotsky, Vasily Bortnikov, Afanasy Kryuk Shobonin, Karp son of Filipp and Vasko son of Pavel Poprikhinsky — and five from Nikolskoye: Ivan son of Ivan Bosovo, Fedko son of Denis, Mikifor son of Semyon Checheyev, Vasko son of Ostash Olekhov and Stepanko Bibik son of Filipp. Also named are Fyodor Zloba son of Dmitry Chyortov and the scribe Popolit Kvashnya son of Dmitry Chyortov. Onfilog, Anfilog or a close patronymic is not among those listed; a separate search for all name variants across the entire available OCR of the volume also gave zero. This is not a census of all households of Priluk, so absence from the boundary representation does not refute the existence of Tonkoi's father, but it eliminates the chance that the sought name literally stood in the published act No. 660. A separate Record PUB-ASEI1-1505-PRILUKI-BOUNDARY-N660 has been created with a map of Priluk and all legible participants. Text of No. 581: https://www.vostlit.info/Texts/Dokumenty/Russ/XIV/1380-1400/Akty_Troic_Serg_mon/581-600/581.htm ; searchable digital copy of ASEI I: https://books.google.com/books?id=xj4aAAAAIAAJ ; regest of No. 660: https://www.vostlit.info/Texts/Dokumenty/Russ/XIV/1380-1400/Akty_Troic_Serg_mon/index.htm .
strings.Полностью проверены географические указа: The geographical indexes of both issues of S. Shumakov's «Тверские акты» ["Tver Acts"] were checked in full. The only Ostrogino, in Yuryev stan, refers to issue 1, pp. 60–61 — the already known deed of gift of Stepan Oskolkov of 1567/1568 with the chain Tsyzyrevs → Oskolkov → the Osipov Monastery. Onfilogovo, Anfilogovo, Beloglazovo, Nikolskoye Svechino and the other stable neighbours of the complex were not found in the index; therefore the collection does not give a new early owner of our settlement. The index did, however, lead to the neighbouring small village of Pervetino in Yuryev stan, pp. 159–160. A deed of purchase of 1571 for Pervetino with its villages states directly that the bond, the testament and the title deeds for the holding burned in the monastery «в приход крымского царя» ["during the incursion of the Crimean tsar"]. This is a documented example of the destruction of the land archive of the immediate area during the invasion of Devlet I Giray. The fire is later than Stefanida's survey and does not explain why she did not present charters in 1551–1554, but it shows a real path for the subsequent loss of acts. A separate Record PUB-TVER-ACTS-1571-P159-160-PERVETINO has been created. Digital issue: https://docs.tverlib.ru/kraevedenie/tverskie_akti_1506_1647_1/ .

"On the Trail of the Trinity Copy Books of the 16th Century" (Po sledam troitskikh kopiynykh knig XVI v.) // Zapiski otdela rukopisey [Notes of the Manuscripts Department]. Issue 40. Moscow, 1979. strings.Полностью получены и распознаны 147 стра: All 147 pages of the edition «Выпись из Тверских писцовых книг. Письма и меры 135 и 136 (1627–1628) годов. Выпуск I» ["Extract from the Tver Scribal Books. Survey and Measurement of the Years 135 and 136 (1627–1628). Issue I"] were obtained in full and OCR-processed from the electronic library of the Tver Regional Library. The first issue prints the first half of the manuscript — the Zakhozhye, Volovitsy and Suzemye stans. The preface literally promises to print the second half in a supplement to the «Тверские епархиальные ведомости» ["Tver Diocesan Gazette"] for 1915 — the Sheksky, Kushalsky, Shostka, Mikulinsky, Goritsky, Khorvatsky and Yuryevsky stans — and then to issue it separately as a second issue. All 48 available PDF issues of the journal for 1915 (Nos. 1–52, with combined numbers) were checked: there is no supplement with the scribal extract in these digital files. A search of the text layer found neither the heading of the extract nor the target toponyms. Thus the second text was announced and probably printed as separate supplements, but these did not enter the modern open set of the journal. Catalogue entry for the first issue: https://elib.tverlib.ru/vypis_iz_tverskih_piscovyh_knig_pisma_i_mery_fedora_ignateva_da_podyachego ; catalogue of the 1915 issues: https://tvereparhia.ru/dejatelnost/tverskie-eparhialnye-vedomosti/ .
