strings.Полностью проверен открытый 349-страничн: The open 349-page reference work was checked in full: A. V. Matison. Dvoryanstvo Tverskogo uyezda XVI – nachala XVIII vekov [The Nobility of Tver Uyezd, 16th – Early 18th Centuries]. Moscow: Drevlekhranilishche, 2023. ISBN 978-5-93646-454-6. On printed p. 320 is the only entry on a Yurlov: «Юрлов Иван (до 1539). Земельные владения: в 1539, 1551 за его женой Стефанидой с. Никольское Свечино и др.» ["Yurlov Ivan (before 1539). Landholdings: in 1539, 1551 held by his wife Stefanida, the village of Nikolskoye Svechino, etc."]. The references lead to the modern edition of the scribal and survey books: Pistsovye materialy Tverskogo uyezda XVI veka [Scribal Materials of Tver Uyezd of the 16th Century]. Moscow, 2005. Pp. 104, 242. In the introduction Matison explains that the formula «до 1539» ["before 1539"] is used for an owner who had already died or is designated as former and is nowhere found alive. This is a weighty research conclusion about Ivan's death before the first entry, but not the literal word «вдова» ["widow"] in the scribal entry. Full open publication: https://www.academia.edu/122950006/ ; page 320: https://attachments.academia-assets.com/117501767/321.html . Paper copies: RGB, shelfmark FB 2 24-26/291; RNB, shelfmark S 2024-2/130.
strings.Сплошной поиск по всем 349 страницам спр: A continuous search through all 349 pages of Matison's reference work yielded only one Yurlov of Tver uyezd — Ivan, the former owner of Nikolskoye Svechino. His patronymic, rank, membership of a particular branch of the Pleshcheyevs and the name of the eponym Onfilog are not given in the entry. Consequently, the most recent prosopography confirms the local chain Ivan Yurlov → his wife Stefanida → Nikolskoye Svechino, but does not allow a choice between Ivan Timofeyevich the Elder and Ivan Timofeyevich the Younger and does not name the founder of the village.
strings.Тот же сплошной просмотр выявил другое о: The same continuous review revealed another settlement of the same name: on printed p. 151, in the entry on Stepan Afanasyevich Likharev, among his holdings of 1588 is recorded «дрв. Онфилогово Чагримово тож» ["the village of Onfilogovo, also called Chagrimovo"]; the source is a separate book of 1588, Pistsovye materialy Tverskogo uyezda XVI veka [Scribal Materials of Tver Uyezd of the 16th Century]. Pp. 564–565. This is a separate toponym with the double name Chagrimovo, whereas our Onfilogovo in 1539/1540 and 1551–1554 belongs to the Nikolskoye Svechino complex together with Sadykovo, Ishkovo, Ostrogino, Voronino and Popovo. The find requires rejecting any later "Onfilogovo" without checking the neighbours and the owner.
strings.Второе раннее точное название найдено в: A second early exact name was found in a grand-princely boundary charter of about 16 June 1504. In the document of Ivan III for Prince Yury Ivanovich, in the description of the Klin–Ruza boundary, «деревня Онфилогова» ["the village of Onfilogova"] is literally named. The reading was verified visually on printed p. 401 of the edition Dukhovnye i dogovornye gramoty velikikh i udelnykh knyazey XIV–XVI vv. [Testaments and Treaty Charters of the Grand and Appanage Princes of the 14th–16th Centuries] (Moscow–Leningrad, 1950), act No. 96, and not only from the OCR. This is not our settlement: the charter relates to the Ruza land and does not contain Nikolskoye Svechino, the Yurlovs, Khorvachi or the Tver neighbours. But the date is crucial: the exact form Onfilogova already existed independently by 1504. Consequently, the name was common enough to give rise to more than one toponym, and the rarity of the word in itself can no longer serve as an argument for identifying the Tver eponym with the father of Tonkoi of Priluk. To distinguish them, the uyezd, the owners and the stable set of neighbours are required.
strings.Нулевой результат в сервисе Яндекса «Пои: The zero result in Yandex's "Search in Archives" service for the queries «Онфилогово» ["Onfilogovo"], «Никольское Свечино» ["Nikolskoye Svechino"] and the shelfmark 1209/16081 cannot be considered a check of RGADA: RGADA is absent from the service's published catalogue of sources. The eleven matches found for "Nikolskoye Svechino" relate to other places of the same name.
strings.24 августа 2026 года отдельно проверен н: On 24 August 2026 a new full-text search engine over the official PDF inventories of RGADA, indexing 67,263 pages, was checked separately. Within f. 1209 the queries «Онфилогово» ["Onfilogovo"], «Анфилогово» ["Anfilogovo"], «Белоглазово» ["Beloglazovo"] and the exact query «Микита Старков» ["Mikita Starkov"] gave no substantive matches. The word «Старков» ["Starkov"] yielded only an unrelated Ivan Starkov, a clerk (podyachy) of the Dorogobuzh court villages, in op. 1, pt. 2, d. 623; «Юрлов» ["Yurlov"] yielded a later disputed case of the heirs of S. A. Yurlov of 1741 in op. 83. These results do not replace an examination of d. 16081: the manuscript register itself, which contains entry No. 272 on Anfilogovo/Beloglazovo and Mikita Starkov, is not included in the full-text PDF corpus. Service checked: https://rgada.sovadev.pro/ .
strings.24 августа 2026 года проверен актуальный: On 24 August 2026 the current catalogue of digitised files of the GIS UIAD (State Information System "Unified Information Space of Archival Documents") was checked. For RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, the catalogue shows 547 available digital entries; the file selector covers early numbers up to d. 536 and d. 539. The target Tver books, dd. 872, 875, 16057, 16060, 16081, 16083, 16086 and 16087, are absent from the available set. Consequently, the full text of entries Nos. 271–272 cannot be obtained through the current paid hourly GIS UIAD session: the file must first be added to the system or ordered directly from RGADA. Catalogue checked: https://metrics.tilda.ws/gisuiad ; official portal: https://online.archives.ru/ .
strings.В базе «Служилые люди» проекта «Дом пред: In the "Service People" database of the «Дом предков» ["House of Ancestors"] project (421,095 entries), a separate search yielded 159 bearers of the form Starkov and 118 bearers of the form Yurlov. The database did not show an exact "Starkov Mikita" or the combination "Yurlov Semyon/Semen". Among the general matches there are people from Moscow, Beloozero, Kursk, Nizhny Novgorod and other places, but not a single row links them to Anfilogovo, Beloglazovo or Nikolskoye Svechino. Therefore the namesakes have not been added as relatives: the check is useful as a limited negative result, not as proof that Mikita or Semyon is absent from other sources. Database: https://next-fast-table-gold.vercel.app/ .
strings.Статья № 272 об Анфилогове локализована: Entry No. 272 on Anfilogovo has been located within d. 16081 by two independent page anchors. In the official inventory, entry No. 13 concerns the pomestye of Mikhail son of Aleksei Yepishev; a published prosopographical index gives for the same record RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, d. 16081, l. 30 and a parallel copy, d. 875, l. 27 v. The second point: entry No. 348 on the vacant lands of Kurman and Danila, sons of Sharap Maslov, is cited from d. 16081, ll. 354 v.–355. Interpolation between entries Nos. 13 and 348 places No. 272 at about l. 281. This is a calculated range, not an already-read foliation of the entry; for an archival order it is safe to request ll. 279–283, including the neighbouring entry No. 271 of Tretyak Starkov and the beginning of the following entry. Sources of the anchors: https://62info.ru/history/node/10930 ; https://geraldika.ru/files/pdf/24081208463929353.pdf .
strings.Официальная современная опись фонда экон: The official modern inventory of the fond of economic notes fully corrects the earlier erroneous reference "f. 1355, op. 1, dd. 18–20". The economic notes on 1,201 dachas (land allotments) of Zubtsov uyezd, together with the alphabetical indexes of dachas and owners, form a single file: RGADA, f. 1355, op. 1, d. 1694, 141 folios, microfilm. The separate dd. 1695 and 1696 are auxiliary alphabetical indexes (35 folios) and a table (1 folio). For dacha No. 516, d. 1694 should be ordered first of all; d. 1695 is useful to order in addition for quickly finding the owner. Source checked against the official 2025 RGADA PDF inventory, PDF page 124: http://rgada.info/opisi/1355-opis_1.pdf .
strings.Непосредственно перед Анфилоговом официа: Immediately before Anfilogovo, the official inventory of d. 16081 places entry No. 271: «поместье Третьяка Старкова» ["the pomestye of Tretyak Starkov"], followed by entry No. 272: «поместье Микиты Старкова, пустошь Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["the pomestye of Mikita Starkov, the waste land Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"]. An earlier report of Simeon Bekbulatovich with a service list of 4 June 1585 names two Tver deti boyarskie: Kolmak son of Ivan Starkov, with an allotment of 250 chetverts and 10 roubles, and Tretyak son of Ivan Starkov, with an allotment of 150 chetverts and 8 roubles. The identical patronymic and family designation make them probable brothers; a scholarly onomastic article also treats them as possible brothers, but the list itself does not use the word "brothers". Tretyak of entry No. 271 is with high probability the same Tver service man of 1585 or a namesake member of the same family. Mikita may have been his younger brother, son or another relative, but the brief inventory gives no patronymic. It is precisely the full text of the neighbouring entries Nos. 271–272 that must test this connection. Service list: https://www.vostlit.info/Texts/Dokumenty/Russ/XVI/1560-1580/Akty_Popov_I/21-40/30.htm ; discussion of the two Starkovs: https://www.drevnyaya.ru/vyp/2014_3/part_13.pdf .
strings.Справочник А. В. Матисона даёт следующий: A. V. Matison's reference work gives the next documented stage of the ownership chain. The entry «Куракин Григорий Семенович, князь» ["Kurakin Grigory Semenovich, Prince"] lists his votchina of 1677: the village of Mikulino-Gorodishche, the hamlet attached to Spasskoye, the village of Oshurkovo and villages, among which Beloglazovo stands explicitly. The author's reference leads to the census book of Tver and Tver uyezd of 1677–1678: RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, d. 16060, ll. 319 v.–348; in addition, the 1710 complex is cited, d. 16086, ll. 320, 348. Thus, after the pomestye of Mikita Starkov, a new established owner of the same place under its later name appears: the boyar Prince Grigory Semyonovich Kurakin. The preceding act has now also been found: on 21 August 1655 a transfer book lists, in the complex sold by Ivan Andreyevich Golitsyn, «деревню Белоглазова на реке на Ржати» ["the village of Beloglazova on the river Rzhat"]; it was precisely this complex that was transferred to Kurakin. This is not the founder and not the eponym: the name Onfilogovo is older than the prince by more than a century. The find refines the archival order — in d. 16060 one should search not the whole volume blindly, but Kurakin's ownership entry on ll. 319 v.–348, where the full text may name the households and peasants of Beloglazovo. Sources: A. V. Matison. Dvoryanstvo Tverskogo uyezda XVI – nachala XVIII vekov [The Nobility of Tver Uyezd, 16th – Early 18th Centuries]. Moscow: Drevlekhranilishche, 2023. P. 144, n. 3; Mikulinskaya letopis, sostavlennaya po drevnim aktam ot 1354 do 1678 goda [The Mikulino Chronicle, Compiled from Ancient Acts from 1354 to 1678]. Tver, 1911. Printed pp. 72–75; https://docs.tverlib.ru/kraevedenie/mikulinskaja_letopis.pdf .
strings.В опубликованной по древним актам Микули: In the Mikulino Chronicle, published from ancient acts, the full list of villages from the transfer book of 21 August 1655 was found. Among them is literally recorded «деревня Белоглазова на реке на Ржати» ["the village of Beloglazova on the river Rzhat"]. This is the first piece of evidence found that does not merely name Beloglazovo but indicates its river. The modern village of Beloglazovo stands on the Rzhat, so the act independently and very strongly confirms moving the marker precisely here. Unlike the record from after 1634/1635, where Anfilogovo/Beloglazovo was a waste land, in 1655 the place is already called a village: by this time it had been resettled or had at least regained the administrative status of a village. The act arose from the sale by Ivan Andreyevich Golitsyn of Mikulino, Oshurkovo and dependent settlements to Prince Grigory Semyonovich Kurakin; the formal transfer took place on 21 August 1655. Source: Mikulinskaya letopis, sostavlennaya po drevnim aktam ot 1354 do 1678 goda [The Mikulino Chronicle, Compiled from Ancient Acts from 1354 to 1678]. Tver, 1911. Printed pp. 72–75, digital PDF pp. 73–76; https://docs.tverlib.ru/kraevedenie/mikulinskaja_letopis.pdf .
strings.В одном и том же акте 1655 года перечисл: One and the same act of 1655 lists two different objects with the same name. First, among the inhabited villages, stands «деревня Белоглазова на реке на Ржати» ["the village of Beloglazova on the river Rzhat"]; later, among the waste lands, «пустошь Белоглазова» ["the waste land Beloglazova"] is recorded separately. They must not be merged. Our Onfilogovo corresponds to the village on the Rzhat: this agrees with the existing village of Beloglazovo and with the later label «д. Онфилогова» ["village of Onfilogova"] next to Voronina on the General Land Survey plan. The separate waste land Beloglazova belongs to another place within the enormous Mikulino–Oshurkovo votchina. In an act of 1645 there also occurs «старая Глазова» ["old Glazova"]; without boundaries and a full comparison it, too, cannot automatically be identified with either of the two Beloglazovas.
strings.Научная историко-географическая ГИС Твер: The scholarly historical-geographical GIS of Tver State University reveals the population of Beloglazovo in the census of 1677/1678. In the layer "Karelians of Tver Uyezd 1677/78" the record has the fields: name — Beloglazovo; uyezd — Tver; volost — Mikulino stan; owner — Prince Grigory Semyonovich Kurakin; land type — votchina; people — 39; households — 1. The coordinates of the research point itself — 35.2414481, 56.3171521 — almost exactly coincide with the corrected marker of the modern village. One household with 39 recorded people should be understood cautiously: it may have been a large composite household community or a peculiarity of census recording, not a modern small family. The names of these 39 people are not given in the published layer; they must be taken from Kurakin's ownership entry in RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, d. 16060, ll. 319 v.–348. Sources: A. I. Savinova, Yu. V. Stepanova, "The Settlement of the Tver Karelians in the 17th–19th Centuries: An Attempt at Study Using GIS Technologies" (Rasseleniye tverskikh karel v XVII–XIX vv.: opyt izucheniya s primeneniyem GIS-tekhnologiy); archived copy of the official GIS https://web.archive.org/web/20240506165035id_/http://karely.histgeo.ru/layers/167778_6.js .
strings.Белоглазово снова нанесено в отдельном с: Beloglazovo is again plotted in a separate layer of the same scholarly GIS, "Mikulino Karelians 1710". The fields of the record confirm Tver uyezd, Mikulino stan and the same point 35.2414481, 56.3171521; the population and the owner are not published in this layer. The creators of the GIS name as the source of the layer the 1710 census book RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, d. 16086. This proves the presence of a Karelian population in Beloglazovo in two time slices separated by about 33 years, but does not prove that each family remained unchanged: personal continuity requires the household-by-household name entries of both censuses. Archived copy of the layer: https://web.archive.org/web/20240506165025id_/http://karely.histgeo.ru/layers/1710_8.js .
strings.Карельские жители Белоглазова 1677/1678: The Karelian inhabitants of Beloglazovo in 1677/1678 and 1710 are a most important later chapter in the history of the village, but not candidates for the founder of Onfilogovo. The name «Онфилогово» ["Onfilogovo"] is documented as early as 1539/1540, that is, at least 137 years before the first Karelian census. Even if the full 1677 list yields dozens of personal names, among them one should look for inhabitants and possibly ancestors of the later population, not for the man from whom the toponym arose. The eponym Onfilog must belong to an earlier layer — most probably to the 15th or the very beginning of the 16th century.
strings.Иван Андреевич Голицын теперь установлен: Ivan Andreyevich Golitsyn is now established as Kurakin's immediate predecessor in the ownership complex that included the relevant village of Beloglazova on the Rzhat. According to the Mikulino Chronicle, he and his wife Feodosia Andreyevna redeemed the former votchina of the Princes Mikulinsky from the Kirillov Monastery and then sold Mikulino and Oshurkovo with their villages to Prince Grigory Semyonovich Kurakin. The transfer record of 21 August 1655 already includes Beloglazova on the Rzhat. However, the published account does not prove that this particular village belonged to the earlier monastery holding or to Fyodor Andreyevich Telyatevsky: a reliable personal chain for the village itself begins here only with Golitsyn and the sale of 1655. The transition from the pomestye of Mikita Starkov after 1634/1635 to Golitsyn's ownership has still not been found.
strings.Полная проверка справочника Матисона под: A complete check of Matison's reference work confirms a separate Tver Onfilogovo, which must not be confused with ours. Under Stepan Afanasyevich Likharev in 1588 the following are listed: the villages Volkovo, «Онфилогово Чагримово тож» ["Onfilogovo, also called Chagrimovo"], Borikhino also called Martyanovo, Padaltsovo, Osanovo also called Volotskoye, and a waste land; the pomestye was separated off in 1588. Source: the separate 1588 book on the pomestyes of the syn boyarsky servitors of Tver uyezd, in the publication «Писцовые материалы Тверского уезда XVI века» ["Scribal Materials of Tver Uyezd, 16th Century"], pp. 564–565. The match of the double name with manuscript entry No. 161 of the 1667/1668 transfer book proves that the act in d. 16065 belongs to the Onfilogovo/Chagrimovo line, not to Onfilogovo/Beloglazovo. The distinguishing key is now strict: our place is accompanied by Beloglazovo, Nikolskoye Svechino, Sadykovo, Ishkovo, Voronino and Popovo; the other one by Chagrimovo and Likharev's holding.
strings.Проверена ревизская сказка 1782 года сел: The 1782 revision tale of the village (selo) of Pervitino has been checked: GATO, f. 312, op. 6, d. 100; FamilySearch, film 2043614, DGS 5363904, internal pages 168–187 (approximately frames 750–769). The heading assigns Pervitino to the holding of the late captain-lieutenant of the Life Guards Izmailovsky Regiment Pyotr Semyonovich Khlopov; the village (derevnya) of Bogdanishnaya is recorded after the selo. Onfilogovo and Voronino do not appear in this tale. Therefore their chain of ownership cannot be automatically traced through the Khlopovs merely because of proximity to Pervitino. In 1782 Pervitino was still counted in Tver uyezd; the area's later assignment to Zubtsov uyezd must not be projected backwards without a caveat.
strings.Полностью проверены внутренние описи дву: The internal inventories of two adjacent collections of revision tales of Tver uyezd have been fully checked: GATO, f. 312, op. 6, d. 102 and 103; FamilySearch, film 2043616, DGS 5363906, frames 217–232 and 691–707. The names Onfilogovo, Anfilogovo, Anpilogovo, Ampilogovo, Svechino and their obvious variants were not found in the lists. The negative result applies only to these two files and does not prove that the village disappeared.
strings.Установлен и просмотрен точный цифровой: The exact digital set of confession registers has been identified and examined: GATO, f. 160, op. 1, d. 16855, 1741; FamilySearch, films 2374526–2374527, DGS 5196004–5196005. File 16855 begins at frame 503 of the first film, so the numbers in the research index must be counted within the file. Pervitino is given on internal page 248, Sadykovo on 258. The section «Никольское» ["Nikolskoye"] on internal page 475 continues already on DGS 5196005; its heading explicitly assigns this Nikolskoye to Zakhozhsky stan. This is a different place of the same name, not Nikolskoye Svechino of Volovitsky stan, and its inhabitants or clergy must not be used in the Onfilogovo card.

strings.Проверен целиком открытый 364-страничный: The openly available 364-page OCR PDF «Писцовые книги XVI века. Тверской уезд. Распознанный текст» ["Scribal Books of the 16th Century. Tver Uyezd. Recognized Text"] from the VGD publication has been checked in full: https://disk.yandex.ru/d/YHq90DVnY70r0Q (159124482 bytes; SHA-256 91ddb3e57f344930f4072a7ec625e8e652ff393a4ae2575f923ff6490f9092d6). A search for the forms Onfilog, Onpilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Ampilog, Amfilog, Svechino and Yurlov found only the two already known entries: p. 111 from the 1539/1540 description and p. 230 from the 1551–1554 survey. They have been visually verified against the page images. The late-16th-century book included in the same PDF describes the lands of Simeon Bekbulatovich in other listed volosts and does not cover Khorvach, so the absence of Onfilogovo there does not prove that the village disappeared.
strings.Проведён сплошной полнотекстовый поиск п: A continuous full-text search has been carried out across the four volumes of «Акты служилых землевладельцев XV — начала XVII века» ["Acts of Service Landholders, 15th – Early 17th Century"] (compiled by A. V. Antonov). In volume I the complete 430-page PDF was checked; in volumes II–IV the available full texts and the name and geographical indexes. The forms Onfilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Ampilog, Onfilogovo, Anfilogovo and Svechino were not found in relation to the Tver holding in question; matches for «Панфилов» ["Panfilov"] were excluded as different names. Volume IV mentions Aleksei and Fyodor Yurlov, but their acts do not connect the family with Nikolskoye Svechino. This negative result narrows the published corpus of acts, but it does not replace Stefanida's unproduced charters or the unpublished RGADA files. Description of the series: https://bibl-kostroma.ru/книги-сборники-альманахи/а .
strings.24 августа 2026 года полностью проверены: On 24 August 2026 the name and geographical indexes of the edition «Акты Троицкого Калязина монастыря XVI в.» ["Acts of the Trinity Kalyazin Monastery, 16th Century"] (Moscow; St Petersburg, 2007, 248 pp.) were fully checked. The forms sought, Onfilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Amfilog, the surnames Svechin and Yurlov, and the names Nikolskoye Svechino and Beloglazovo do not occur in the published corpus. The index reveals a different person, Onfim Negodyai Ushakov's son (act No. 132); his name Onfim is phonetically close to the beginning of «Онфилог» ["Onfilog"], but it is an independent calendar name and cannot be turned into Onfilog without direct evidence. The book also has the grand-princely village of Onfimova at the borders of the Kalyazin Monastery's lands (printed p. 134), which clearly confirms the formation of possessive place names from a personal name, but it relates to a different name and to Kashin geography. The negative result matters because the publication covers real 16th-century Tver acts and landholders. S. N. Popov's reference «РГАДА. Ф. 1193. Оп. 1. № 31—33. Вкладная книга» ["RGADA. F. 1193. Op. 1. Nos. 31–33. Donation book"] is printed exactly like this in the scan of the dissertation abstract, but it does not match the modern official inventory of the fonds; until the archive decodes it, it must not be arbitrarily turned either into separate files 31–33 or into folios 31–33 of file 1. Open volume: https://aarheo.ru/files/Kalyazin.pdf ; library record: https://aarheo.ru/library ; scan of S. N. Popov's dissertation abstract: https://www.prlib.ru/item/372777 .
strings.Скан печатного автореферата С. Н. Попова: The scan of S. N. Popov's printed dissertation abstract in the Presidential Library confirms the literal reference twice: «РГАДА. Ф. 1193. Оп. 1. № 31—33. Вкладная книга Троицкого Калязина монастыря» ["RGADA. F. 1193. Op. 1. Nos. 31–33. Donation book of the Trinity Kalyazin Monastery"]. Consequently, this is not an OCR error in a web copy. At the same time the modern official inventory shows that the separate files 31, 32 and 33 are dated 1852–1858, have 955, 1072 and 852 folios, and are described as decrees, registers and miscellaneous monastic matters — they are not an ancient donation book. File 1 does contain donation, grant, purchase and boundary charters of the 15th–17th centuries on 266 folios, but there are as yet no data allowing Popov's «№ 31—33» ["Nos. 31–33"] to be confidently interpreted as ll. 31–33 of file 1. Possible explanations are an old or internal numbering of the manuscripts, a later reworking of the inventory, or an inaccuracy in Popov's archival shelfmark itself. Therefore the safe next step is to ask RGADA to identify Popov's citation and give its modern shelfmark, enclosing the page of the abstract; the present dd. 31–33 or d. 1, ll. 31–33 must not be ordered as an already established donation book. Official inventory: http://rgada.info/opisi/1193-opis_1.pdf ; fonds record: http://rgada.info/poisk/index.php?fund_number=1193&fund_name=&list_number=&list_name=&Sk=100&B1=Найти ; printed scan of the abstract: https://www.prlib.ru/item/372777 .
strings.Введение к научному изданию «Акты Троицк: The introduction to the scholarly edition «Акты Троицкого Калязина монастыря XVI в.» ["Acts of the Trinity Kalyazin Monastery, 16th Century"] (Moscow–St Petersburg, 2007) clarifies the physical arrangement of the modern complex. RGADA, f. 1193, op. 1, kn. 1 is a volume of 266 folios artificially assembled by later archivists: it combines original acts, 16th–18th-century copies and fragments of a copy book. Kn. 4 is another composite volume of 490 folios: acts occupy ll. 1–290 and 469–482, extracts from scribal books ll. 291–408, and two 18th-century archival inventories ll. 409–468. The contents of books 1 and 4 partly overlap. This explains why a single old document could have several levels of numbering — the number of an individual act, the folio within the bound volume and a later archival shelfmark — but it does not yet prove which level Popov meant by Nos. 31–33. The editors also report that searches for additional acts in GATO and the Tver Museum produced no result. Source: «Акты Троицкого Калязина монастыря XVI в.» ["Acts of the Trinity Kalyazin Monastery, 16th Century"], comp. S. N. Kisterev, L. A. Timoshina. Moscow–St Petersburg: Alyans-Arkheo, 2007, introduction, description of the manuscript tradition; digital copy: https://aarheo.ru/files/Kalyazin.pdf .
strings.Старые описания монастырского собрания п: Old descriptions of the monastery's collection are checked separately from the corpus of acts itself. The virtual exhibition of the Tver Regional Library confirms that the «Краткая опись» ["Brief Inventory"] by Hieromonk Pavel (Krylov), Kalyazin, 1900, describes 354 patriarchal, metropolitan and episcopal charters of the 17th century only, dated 1614–1683. This is not the 15th–16th-century donation book being sought and not a likely source for the name of Onfilogovo's founder. The five-page fragment of Pavel Krylov's 1897 book made available by the library contains only title pages and views of the monastery; there is no archival numbering in it. The full-text copy of A. E. Viktorov's 1890 inventory gives an important negative and at the same time structural result. In July 1880 Viktorov saw only ten manuscripts in the library and sacristy: three of the 15th, three of the 16th, three of the 17th and one of the 18th century; none of them is called a donation book in the description. For comparison, the 1653 inventory counted 24 manuscripts, of which by 1880 Viktorov confidently matched only two miscellanies. He described the archive separately: item 5 — 102 acts of the 18th century, item 6 — about 250 acts of the 16th–18th centuries in old copies, bound into a book of about 500 folios; the originals of most of these acts were included in the preceding volumes. This structure closely resembles the later composite volumes described in the 2007 edition and explains the possibility of an internal numbering of acts, but it does not reveal a separate donation book Nos. 31–33. A. N. Lebedev's 1867 description and I. F. Golubev's 1960 museum note remain unchecked. Sources: https://projects.tverlib.ru/makary_kalyazinsky/ ; A. E. Viktorov, «Описи рукописных собраний в книгохранилищах Северной России» ["Inventories of Manuscript Collections in the Repositories of Northern Russia"], St Petersburg, 1890, pp. 279–284, digital copy: https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/books/file/30293-Описи-рукописных-собраний-в-книгохранилищах-северной-России.pdf ; NEB record: https://rusneb.ru/catalog/000199_000009_003551382/ .
strings.Актуальный выгружаемый каталог ГИС УИАД: The current downloadable catalogue of the GIS UIAD has been checked separately for the RGADA archive: there are no records of fonds 1193 in the available online set, so file 1 and the supposed ll. 31–33 cannot be opened through the current hourly viewing service. The file remains accessible only through the reading room or by ordering copies from RGADA. This is a check of the availability catalogue, not of the contents of the folios. Catalogue: https://metrics.tilda.ws/gisuiad ; official portal: https://online.archives.ru/ .
strings.Полностью проверена цифровая копия публи: The digital copy of I. A. Ivanov's publication «Кормовая книга Колязина монастыря» ["The Feast Book of the Kolyazin Monastery"] (published 1891/1892, 34 digital pages) has been checked in full. The text describes donations and commemorations mainly from 1610 onward; the forms Onfilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Amfilog, Yurlov, Svechin, Beloglaz, Nikolskoye Svechino and the stable cluster of Stefanida's villages were not found in it. Consequently, the late feast book has not preserved an obvious commemorative bridge to the eponym being sought. This negative result does not extend to the ancient charters of file 1 and the supposed folios 31–33: these are different complexes. Digital copy: https://docs.tverlib.ru/kraevedenie/lb0000882/ ; library record: https://elib.tverlib.ru/kormovaya_kniga_kolyazina_monastyrya_s_predisloviem_chlena_tverskoy_uchenoy_arhivnoy_komissii_i .
strings.Постранично проверена дореволюционная «О: The pre-revolutionary «Опись древним грамотам и другим документам, хранящимся в архиве первоклассного Троицкого Калязинского монастыря» ["Inventory of Ancient Charters and Other Documents Kept in the Archive of the First-Class Trinity Kalyazin Monastery"] (Tver, 1891, 36 pp.) has been checked page by page. Onfilog, Anfilog, the Yurlovs, the Svechins, Nikolskoye Svechino or Beloglazovo were not found in the list of 15th–16th-century charters. On the other hand, the inventory makes it possible to date the unrelated Onfimova precisely: No. 121 — an exchange deed of the monastery's village of Pankratovo for the village of Onfimovo, 1542; No. 141 — a copy of the reverse exchange of the village of Onfimova for Pankratovo, 1552. This confirms that Onfimova was an independent object of a land transaction and is not a misreading of Onfilogovo. Nearby in the catalogue there are a 1527 deed of purchase for a different village (selo) of Nikolskoye in Kashin uyezd (No. 65) and a 1528 boundary division of the village of Voronino with the new clearing Popadyino (No. 71); coincidences of individual common names without the whole stable cluster Nikolskoye Svechino — Sadykovo — Ishkovo — Ostrogino — Voronino — Popovo do not connect these acts with Stefanida's holding. Digital copy: https://docs.tverlib.ru/kraevedenie/lb0000377/ ; library record: https://elib.tverlib.ru/opisi_drevnim_gramotam_i_drugim_dokumentam_hranyashchimsya_v_arhive_pervoklassnogo_troickogo .
strings.В купчей августа 1516 года на четверть д: In a deed of purchase of August 1516 for a quarter of the village of Titovskaya, two different bearers of the relevant name stem are named at once. Maksim Nesterov sold land that he had earlier bought «у Анфилофья у Иванова сына» ["from Anfilofy, Ivan's son"]; among the witnesses (poslukhi) of the same transaction «Анфилоф Мосеев сын» ["Anfilof, Mosei's son"] is recorded. The first Anfilofy was the previous owner of the share of the village, the second Anfilof a participant in attesting the transaction. The act belongs to the northern Russian complex of the Antoniev-Siysky Monastery and has no connection with Tver uyezd, so neither of the two men becomes the founder of Onfilogovo. The find matters in another way: it shows that the forms Anfilofy/Anfilof were indeed used as personal names of landholders and participants in land transactions in exactly the generation when the Tver place name arose. The simultaneous presence of two men of the same name also weakens the earlier argument from exceptional rarity: a single coincidence of name and time is not enough without a geographical or ownership bridge. Primary digital publication of the St Petersburg Institute of History, RAS: https://gis.spbiiran.ru/cyrillic/cyrillic-alphabet-1217/acts/1153 .
strings.В судной грамоте по спору Рязанского Оль: In a judicial charter on the dispute between the Ryazan Olgov Monastery and Fyodor Kartsov, dated by the publication to the 1530s, among the participants of the sovereign's inquest there is explicitly named «из великого князя села ис подклетного и Старотумова крестьянин Анфилог Иванов сын Констянтинова» ["from the grand prince's household village and from Starotumovo, the peasant Anfilog Ivanov son of Konstyantinov"]. The inquest officer Timofei Aigustov questioned 43 syn boyarsky servitors, clergy and peasants as to whom the village of Ruposovo belonged, who had set it up and how many years it had existed; Anfilog was in the group that confirmed, on kissing the cross, the old ownership of the Olgov Monastery. This is the first direct peasant found with the full form Anfilog, exactly contemporary with the Tver entry and appearing in proceedings about the origin of a village. But the document belongs to Ryazan uyezd and does not name Nikolskoye Svechino, the Yurlovs or the Tver volost of Khorvach, so the man serves as the strongest social parallel, not as an established eponym. Archival address of the publication: RGADA, f. 1199, op. 1, No. 118, l. 200–220 ob.; the name on l. 212; publication «Памятники Рязанского края» ["Monuments of the Ryazan Land"], No. 61, pp. 88–95; open text: https://m.62info.ru/history/node/10631 .
strings.Та же рязанская судная грамота даёт редк: The same Ryazan judicial charter gives a rare literal example of how a 16th-century document established the founder and eponym of a settlement. Witnesses testified that Karets Kurdumov and his son Fyodor «ту деревню поставили» ["set up that village"], though they differed on how long ago: seven, six or four years. Separately, about an old abandoned settlement it is said: «словет ... то селищо Митусово потому, что жил на том селище конюх Митус» ["that old settlement is called Mitusovo because the groom Mitus lived on that settlement"]. Here the man, his occupation and the reason for the place name are named together. This is not the history of the Tver Onfilogovo, but an exact comparative model of the evidence being sought: to complete the search, the same kind of line is needed — who set up the village, or why the place is called Onfilogovo. The source's caution also matters: the testimonies about the recent founding diverged, and Fyodor tried to extend the old name Mitusovo to his disputed homestead. Consequently, even a direct formula must be read together with the boundaries, the right to the land and independent witnesses. Open full text: https://m.62info.ru/history/node/10631, l. 211–214 according to the publication.
strings.24 августа 2026 года через публичный Gra: On 24 August 2026 the public GraphQL search of the GIS of the St Petersburg Institute of History, RAS, was used to check the personal forms Onfilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Ampilog, Amfilog, Anfilof, Anfilofy and Amfilokhy, as well as the broad beginnings Anfi-, Onfi-, Amfi-, Anpi-, Onfo- and Anfo-. The exact nest Anfilof yielded only three indexed people: Anfilofy Ivanov's son and Anfilof Moseyev's son in a single northern deed of purchase of 1516, and Anfilofy Ontrofyev's son in a deed of purchase for holdings in the village of Klimovskaya, 1562. The last is too late and is also unconnected with Tver. No persons with the forms Onfilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Ampilog or Amfilog were found in the index. This is a negative result within a single scholarly database, not proof that the person is absent from the unpublished Tver books.
strings.Главный новый заказ — полный оригинал ил: The main new order is the complete original or the closest copy of the transfer book of 21 August 1655, published in «Микулинская летопись» ["The Mikulino Chronicle"] on pp. 72–75. The printed list has already given the exact formula «деревня Белоглазова на реке на Ржати» ["the village of Beloglazova on the river Rzhat"], but the household names are omitted in the extract. It is necessary to establish the modern archival shelfmark of the act and order all folios of the entry: the peasants' names, the basis of Ivan Andreyevich Golitsyn's tenure, the previous holder, the formula of sale to Kurakin and the boundaries. Particular care is needed to distinguish two identically named items in one act — the inhabited village of Beloglazova on the Rzhat and a separate waste land of Beloglazova. Second, narrow order: RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, ch. 2, d. 16081, calculated ll. 279–283. The full entries No. 271 «поместье Третьяка Старкова» ["the pomestye of Tretyak Starkov"] and No. 272 «поместье Микиты Старкова, пустошь Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["the pomestye of Mikita Starkov, the waste land Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"] are needed, including the versos of the folios. Elements sought: Mikita's patronymic, the previous owner of Anfilogovo, the formula of the grant, a reference to a charter, the neighbours along the boundaries and the connection with Tretyak Starkov. It is these two orders that should close the gap between Starkov after 1634/1635 and Golitsyn in 1655. Next: economic notes to grant No. 516 «д. Онфилогова» ["the village of Onfilogova"] — RGADA, f. 1355, op. 1, d. 1694; alphabetical list of owners — d. 1695; Kurakin's ownership entry in the 1677/1678 census — f. 1209, op. 1, d. 16060, ll. 319 ob.–348; the 1710 census — dd. 16083, 16086–16087. For the fonds of the Kalyazin Monastery, a reference inquiry is first needed about the modern shelfmark of S. N. Popov's citation «ф. 1193, оп. 1, № 31—33, Вкладная книга» ["f. 1193, op. 1, Nos. 31–33, Donation book"]; the present dd. 31–33 should not be ordered, since they date from the 19th century. In all books check the cluster Nikolskoye Svechino — Sadykovo — Ishkovo — Ostrogino — Voronino — Popovo and exclude the other Onfilogovo also called Chagrimovo.
strings.Н. А. Петровский приводит Амфилох и Амфи: N. A. Petrovsky gives Amfilokh and Amfil as colloquial forms of the name Amfilokhy. V. A. Nikonov specifies that Amfil was also a separate canonical name and that in living speech derivatives of Amfilokhy, Amfil, Ampely and Amply could become mixed. Therefore the reliable conclusion from the place name is the personal form Onfilog/Anfilog/Anpilog; the reconstruction of the full church form Amfilokhy is probable but not absolute. Independent sources name real bearers: the former owner Anpilog Ivanov's son Onanyin, mentioned retrospectively in the Oryol book of 1594/1595, and the peasant Anpilog (Anfilog) Ivanov son of Konstantinov from Ryazan sources.
strings.Н. А. Петровский. Словарь русских личных: N. A. Petrovsky. «Словарь русских личных имён» ["Dictionary of Russian Personal Names"]: the entry «Амфилохий» ["Amfilokhy"] (Amfil, Amfilokh — colloquial forms): https://gramota.ru/biblioteka/slovari/slovar-russkih-imyon ; V. A. Nikonov. «География фамилий» ["The Geography of Surnames"], section on the names Amfil/Amfilokhy and the forms Ampilogov, Amfilogov: https://ruslang.ru/doc/etymology/1971/13-nikonov.pdf ; Alphabetical list of persons of the Ryazan land: Anpilog (Anfilog) Ivanov son of Konstantinov, peasant: https://62info.ru/history/node/9353
strings.Точная статья найдена в РГАДА, ф. 1209,: The exact entry has been found in RGADA, f. 1209, op. 1, kn. 466, l. 183 ob.–184 (digital file reg-num-0406_rgada_1209_1_466_184.jpg). The original confirms: «дер. Онфилогово: 4 дв.» ["the village of Onfilogovo: 4 households"]; the number of households is followed by arable land and hay, and the names of the four householders are absent. The 1877 publication did not omit the household names in this part — they are not in the manuscript.
strings.Иван Тимофеевич Юрлов-Плещеев Большой те: Ivan Timofeyevich Yurlov-Pleshcheyev the Elder (Bolshoi) is now the candidate whose details match best for Stefanida's husband. A. V. Kazakov's study shows that after his flight between 1508 and early 1511 his first wife remained in the Muscovite state; she is mentioned three times in diplomatic documents of 1511–1512 without a personal name; Vasily III never allowed her to leave to join her husband. In Lithuania Ivan married a second time, to Hanna, daughter of Martin Khrebtovich, before January 1516. Ivan is last found alive on 30 January 1529, and in 1532 Hanna was already disposing of his house as her husband's property. This agrees precisely with Matison's conclusion «Юрлов Иван (до 1539)» ["Yurlov Ivan (before 1539)"] and with Stefanida's appearance in 1539 as the holder of Ivan's Russian holding. The rare family name, the marital situation, the first wife's country of residence and the chronology of his death all match. But the first wife is nowhere called Stefanida, and Nikolskoye Svechino is not listed among the known holdings of Ivan the Elder; therefore this is the leading attribution hypothesis, not an established identity.
strings.А. В. Казаков. «За его к нам верную служ: A. V. Kazakov. «„За его к нам верную службу…“: Иван Тимофеевич Юрлов из рода Плещеевых в Великом княжестве Литовском» ["'For His Faithful Service to Us…': Ivan Timofeyevich Yurlov of the Pleshcheyev Family in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania"] // Istorichesky vestnik. 2014. Vol. 7 (154). Pp. 86–113: the first wife in the Muscovite state and the diplomatic requests — pp. 92–93; the second marriage with Hanna Khrebtovich — pp. 100–101; the last mention during his lifetime on 30 January 1529 and Hanna's disposal of the property in 1532 — p. 105; daughters from the second marriage — p. 112. Lithuanian Metrica. Book 7. Vilnius, 2011. Nos. 91, 98.1, 131.2 — three diplomatic mentions of the first wife.
strings.Полное распознавание тома III «Актов соц: Full recognition of volume III of «Акты социально-экономической истории Северо-Восточной Руси» ["Acts of the Socio-Economic History of North-Eastern Rus"] has revealed one more real Anfilof of the eponym's generation — not in person but through his son. Around 1499–1505, in a deed of purchase for the village of Krasnikova in Zhabensky stan of Kashin uyezd, «Пешок Анфилофов сын Лодыгина» ["Peshok, Anfilof's son, of Lodygin"] is named; he was a witness and signed the charter with his own hand. Around 1505–1510 Peshok himself wrote another deed of purchase, and in 1515/1516 he again acted as a witness. His patronymic attests a real Anfilof of the older generation, probably living in the 15th century. This is the first trace of such a father found within the Kashin circle of land acts of the Tver land, so it is geographically more meaningful than the Ryazan and northern parallels. However, all three of Peshok's acts belong to Kashin uyezd and to the acts of the Trinity Kalyazin Monastery; Nikolskoye Svechino, the Yurlovs and Onfilogovo are absent from them. The status of the elder Anfilof Lodygin is a new regional candidate, but not an established eponym. Source: ASEI. Vol. III. Moscow: Nauka, 1964. Nos. 169, 174 and the editors' reference to Kalyazin book IV, No. 4; especially pp. 179, 189 and the name index p. 551.
strings.24 августа 2026 года весь 346-страничный: On 24 August 2026 the entire 346-page scan of ASEI, vol. III, which had no text layer, was recognized page by page and checked for the forms Onfilog, Onpilog, Anfilog, Anpilog, Amfilog, Amfilokh, Anfilof, as well as for Yurlov, Inkovo/Ipkovo, Beloglazovo, Svechino and Khorvach. Besides the already known Anfilof Selivanov, the following were found: Peshok Anfilof's son Lodygin from Kashin uyezd and the Ryazan «княж Федоров муж» ["Prince Fyodor's man"] Antipa Anfilog's son Feodotyevskoy from a boundary charter of 1483–1503. No act in the volume connects these people with Nikolskoye Svechino or the Yurlovs. The negative result applies to the entire published volume, not only to the electronic index; the new bearers of the name are kept as candidates and control parallels.
strings.Духовная грамота князя Дмитрия Ивановича: The testament of Prince Dmitry Ivanovich Zhilka, drawn up before 14 February 1521, states: «а у Ивана у Юрлова у меншово купил есми село Инково з деревнями» ["and from Ivan Yurlov the Younger I bought the village of Inkovo with its hamlets"]. The 1950 academic edition and its geographical index print «Инково» ["Inkovo"]; the electronic transcriptions of Vostlit and DrevLit give the variant «Ипково» ["Ipkovo"]. Both readings refer to the same village in Uglich uyezd. Ivan the Younger is most likely the younger brother of Ivan Timofeyevich Yurlov-Pleshcheyev the Elder. In the same Uglich uyezd, Tonkoi Onfilogov is found in 1536/1537. This creates a new search triangle: Yurlov — Uglich — a bearer of the patronymic designation Onfilogov. But Inkovo and Priluki have not yet been brought together into a single ownership complex, the wife of Ivan the Younger is not named, and the transfer of the Tver Nikolskoye Svechino to Stefanida has not been traced.
strings.Духовные и договорные грамоты великих и: Dukhovnye i dogovornye gramoty velikikh i udelnykh knyazei XIV–XVI vv. [Testamentary and Treaty Charters of the Grand and Appanage Princes, 14th–16th Centuries]. Moscow–Leningrad, 1950. No. 99. Pp. 409–415, especially p. 414; RGADA, f. 135, otd. I, rubr. I, No. 35, l. 1–5. First edition: SGGD [Collection of State Charters and Treaties]. Part 1. Moscow, 1813. No. 147. Pp. 405–411. Biographical attribution: A. V. Kazakov. «За его к нам верную службу…» ["For his faithful service to us…"] // Istorichesky vestnik [Historical Herald]. 2014. Vol. 7 (154). Pp. 86–113.
strings.Статья Угличского государственного музея: An article by the Uglich State Museum on the pomestye system erroneously states that Prince Dmitry Zhilka bought the village of Voskresenskoye from Ivan Yurlov Menshoi. The primary published text of the testamentary charter on p. 414 distinguishes two transactions: the hamlet (seltso) of Voskresenskoye was bought from Ivanets Tur Menshoi, and the village of Inkovo with its hamlets from Ivan Yurlov Menshoi. The geographical index of the same academic edition lists Inkovo and Voskresenskoye separately as two villages of Uglich uyezd. Therefore the museum's retelling does not create a new Yurlov holding and must not replace the literal charter. The museum article is useful for the attribution of Ivan Menshoi, but its name of the estate has been corrected from the primary source: https://uglmus.ru/about/publics/pomestnayasistema_copy/ .
strings.Вкладная книга Троице-Сергиева монастыря: Vkladnaya kniga Troitse-Sergiyeva monastyrya [The Donation Book of the Trinity-Sergius Monastery] / ed. prepared by Ye. N. Klitina, T. N. Manushina, T. V. Nikolayeva. Moscow: Nauka, 1987. Section 98 «Род Юрловых» ["The Yurlov Family"], p. 74, manuscript l. 248. Two early entries of the section: on 28 March 1535 a donation by Vasily Bobrov «по Тимофее Юрле и по ево родителех» ["for Timofei Yurla and for his kin"]; on 30 December 1540 the elder Selivestr Stupishin gave 10 rubles «по Петре Иванове сыне Юрлове» ["for Pyotr, son of Ivan, Yurlov"]. The first form shows the original byname Yurla; the second documents Pyotr Ivanovich Yurlov and his death before the date of the donation, but does not name his mother and does not specify which of the two Ivans was his father. Biographical caveat about the two possible fathers: S. B. Veselovsky. Issledovaniya po istorii klassa sluzhilykh zemlevladeltsev [Studies in the History of the Class of Service Landholders]. Moscow: Nauka, 1969. P. 258.
strings.Тимофей Юрла из вкладной записи отождест: Timofei Yurla of the donation entry is identified with Timofei Mikhailovich Pleshcheyev, nicknamed Yurlo, a member of the old Muscovite Pleshcheyev family and an okolnichy of Ivan III. In 1469 he took part in the campaign to Vyatka and Kazan, was captured in battle at the confluence of the Kama and the Volga, and was released on 1 September. Service records confidently extend his life into the 1490s; reference works give dates of death ranging from 1496 to 1504, while the memorial donation establishes only that he was already dead by 28 March 1535. The late dialect meanings of the word «юрло» ["yurlo"] — «силач, драчун» ["strongman, brawler"] — as well as an association with a restless, active person, are kept as possible parallels but are not transferred to the 15th-century individual as a proven characteristic.

Uglichsky uyezd v XVII veke" [The Uglich Scribal Books. Uglich Uyezd in the 17th Century] in the "Vremennik Demidovskogo yuridicheskogo litseya" [Annals of the Demidov Law Lyceum], books 41–46, were fully OCR-processed and checked. The search covered the forms Onfilog, Onfil, Anfilog, Anfil, Anpilog, Amfilog, Anfilof, Lodygin, Yurlov, Inkovo/Ipkovo, Priluki, Svechino, Beloglazovo and Khorvach; doubtful matches were checked against the page images. The village of Inkovo/Ipkovo, bought by Prince Dmitry Zhilka from Ivan Yurlov Menshoi before 1521, was not found in this late scribal book under the expected readings. This is a negative result for the published corpus of 1629/1630, not proof that the village disappeared or that the 16th-century act is erroneous.
strings.В книге 41, печатная с. 101, статья 165,: In book 41, printed p. 101, article 165, among sixteen vacant pomestye lands of the former pomestye of Timofei Ivanov syn Volynsky, it is printed directly: «Пст. Онфиловьево, паш. л. пор. серед. земли 5 чтв. ... сена 5 коп.» ["Waste land Onfilovyevo, ploughland, fallow, of middling land 5 chetverts ... hay 5 kopnas"]. The reading has been checked against the page image. This is the second Uglich toponymic attestation of the rare stem: a separate waste land Onfilovyevo in Gorodskoy stan already existed as a name by 1629/1630. It is not the Tver Onfilogovo: a different uyezd, a different landholding complex, the form Onfilovyevo, and the absence of Nikolskoye Svechino. Its exact modern location within the group of waste lands Turishchevo — Mekhovo — Kononovo — Kobylino has not yet been reconstructed.
strings.Полная проверка угличской книги выявила: The full check of the Uglich book revealed not one but several Lodygins: on printed p. 123 the waste land «Лодыгино, а Ушаково тож» ["Lodygino, also called Ushakovo"] on the Korozhechna is recorded, along with four empty mill sites, including the Lodyzhenskaya mill; in other stans there occur a former hamlet Lodygino, the waste land Porygino «Лодыгино тож» ["also called Lodygino"] and yet another waste land Lodygino. This confirms a noticeable Uglich toponymic trace of the name or family of the Lodygins and makes the Kashin Peshok, son of Anfilof, Lodygin more substantive as a line of research. But the multiplicity of identically named places at the same time forbids automatically linking any of them to Peshok's family or to Priluki. On p. 123 Lodygino belongs to the votchina of Prince Ivan Mikhailovich Katyrev-Rostovsky on the Korozhechna, whereas Priluki is a separate Trinity votchina on the Volga.
strings.Статья 305 писцовой книги 1629/1630 года: Article 305 of the 1629/1630 scribal book on the Trinity village of Priluki has been checked in full on printed pp. 157–195: church households, the monastery household, the cattle yard, nine households of detenyshi [monastery labourers], peasant and bobyl households, empty sites, dependent hamlets, householdless bobyls, and boundaries. In the then-current generation of the village there are no forms Onfilog, Anfilog, Anfil, Lodygin, Yurlov, Svechin or Beloglaz. Tonkoi Onfilogov is known from an earlier entry of 1536/1537, so the absence of his name almost a century later is expected and does not refute the early man; it only shows that the late scribal book did not preserve a direct descendant with the same naming.
strings.По четырём частям исследования С. М. Каш: Using the four parts of S. M. Kashtanov's study "Po sledam troitskikh kopiynykh knig XVI v." [On the Trail of the Trinity Copy Books of the 16th Century], the manuscript basis of the publication of Tonkoi Onfilogov has been fully checked. The extract from the scribal books of Semyon Buturlin and his colleagues occupies a separate block, l. 65–77 ob., in the National Library of Russia (RNB), Pogod. 1846; Tonkoi is named on l. 65 ob. Kashtanov lists this document among texts not known from originals or other copies, i.e. the entry survives in a single known witness. To the copy book of the Trinity-Sergius Monastery No. 518 the researcher returned other Pogodin leaves — 1–10, 16 and 78–85; leaves 65–77 do not belong there and are not identified with book No. 637 in the published series. This removes the earlier assumption that the search for Tonkoi's father could be conducted through the table of contents of book No. 518. The correct next circle is the early acts of the village of Priluki itself and of the neighbouring monastery lands. Publications: Zapiski otdela rukopisei [Notes of the Manuscript Department], issue 38 (1977), pp. 30–63, especially pp. 31–35; issue 40 (1979), pp. 4–58, document No. 3, pp. 43–47; issue 42 (1981), pp. 5–63; issue 43 (1982), pp. 4–37.
strings.Новый прямой носитель основы найден в кн: A new direct bearer of the stem has been found in book 45, printed p. 412, article 107: in the hamlet of Kolyubayevo on the river Vereksa, in the old votchina of Ivan Yuryevich Neledinsky in Rozhalovsky stan, is recorded «во дв. б. Тимошка Анфилов» ["in the household, the bobyl Timoshka Anfilov"]. The line has been checked against the facsimile. Timoshka is Timofei; the abbreviation «б.» means bobyl; Anfilov is a patronymic or already a family naming derived from Anfil. A separate profile P9655 and the record PUB-LIPINSKY-1629-KOLYUBAEVO-TIMOSHKA-ANFILOV have been created for this person. He expands the Uglich name cluster, but he lived in 1629/1630 — almost ninety years after the first record of the Tver Onfilogovo — and therefore cannot be its founder. Kolyubayevo lay by the Vereksa and the Sit in a different landholding complex; the map shows only an approximate reference point in the river basin, not the exact household.
strings.На листах 183 об.—184 тверской книги с О: On leaves 183 ob.–184 of the Tver book with Onfilogovo, the counter-signature (skrepa) of the diak Andrei Myasnov applies. In March 1577 a reply extract of the Pomestny prikaz in a neighbouring case was counter-signed by the diak Andrei Myasnoi; S. B. Veselovsky's reference work identifies him as Andrei Nikitich Sudokov-Myasnoi — a Tula syn boyarsky and tysyachnik of 1550, later a diak of the Pomestnaya izba. The coincidence of a rare name and family naming is unexpected, but identity has not been established: the Tver book gives no patronymic, 38 years separate the documents, and the reference work does not include the Tver counter-signature in the biography of Andrei Nikitich. It can be claimed neither that this is one person nor that the name Onfilogovo is connected through him to Oryol Anfilogovs. The official RGADA digital copy shows that the Storozhevaya kniga [Guard Book] on ll. 223–230 merely copies information about the reply memorandum «за приписью» ["under the endorsement"] of Myasnoi and does not preserve his own autograph signature; comparing the handwriting with the Tver counter-signature on the basis of this copy is impossible. The way to verify this is to find another original act of Andrei Nikitich and to compare the counter-signatures, the early service and the genealogy of the Myasnois. Until proven, this is a palaeographic and biographical lead, not a migration bridge and not a basis for the map.
strings.Чтение «Онфилогово» подтверждено по скан: The reading «Онфилогово» ["Onfilogovo"] has been confirmed from the page scan: the name is set in italics, and the letter «г» ["g"] is clearly visible. The edition's OCR gave the erroneous «Онфилозово» ["Onfilozovo"], and also «Острозино» ["Ostrozino"] instead of «Острогино» ["Ostrogino"]. The continuation of the story has been found in the official RGADA inventory for d. 16081: after 1634/1635 the place is recorded as the waste land «Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"] in the pomestye of Mikita Starkov; the reading of the second name is confirmed by its match with the existing Beloglazovo, 2.42 km from the scholarly reconstruction of the centre of the holding.
strings.ЛЮДИ, НАЗВАННЫЕ В ЗАПИСИ. Формула «за Ст:
PEOPLE NAMED IN THE RECORD. The formula «за Стефанидою за Ивановою женою Юрлова» ["held by Stefanida, wife of Ivan Yurlov"] names the landholder Stefanida and her husband Ivan Yurlov. «Иванова жена» ["Ivan's wife"] means "the wife of Ivan", not Stefanida's patronymic; her own patronymic and maiden name are unknown. The word «вдова» ["widow"] is absent, so the literal line does not report a death directly. However, A. V. Matison, having examined the complex of Tver scribal materials, classifies him as «Юрлов Иван (до 1539)» ["Yurlov Ivan (before 1539)"] — a former owner nowhere found alive — and links Nikolskoye Svechino held by Stefanida to his holding. Most probably Ivan died before 1539, and his wife continued to hold the complex. The form «Юрлова» ["Yurlova"] is the feminine form of the male byname or family name Yurlov. Among the known 16th-century Yurlovs, the best candidate for Stefanida's husband is now Ivan Timofeyevich Yurlov-Pleshcheyev Bolshoi. After his flight to Lithuania his first wife, not named, remained in the Muscovite state and in 1511–1512 figured three times in negotiations for permission to leave and join her husband; Vasily III did not let her go. In Lithuania Ivan married a second time, Hanna Khrebtovich; he was last found alive on 30 January 1529, and in 1532 Hanna was already disposing of his property. This biography matches Stefanida's situation exactly in country and time, but the name of the first wife and her holdings are not revealed. Therefore Ivan Bolshoi is the leading candidate, not a proven husband.

A NEW YURLOV–UGLICH BRIDGE. The testamentary charter of Prince Dmitry Zhilka, drawn up before 14 February 1521, says: «а у Ивана у Юрлова у меншово купил есми село Инково з деревнями» ["and from Ivan Yurlov Menshoi I bought the village of Inkovo with its hamlets"]. The 1950 academic edition and its geographical index twice print «Инково» ["Inkovo"] and assign it to Uglich uyezd; the electronic transcriptions on Vostlit and DrevLit give the variant «Ипково» ["Ipkovo"]. In the same Uglich uyezd in 1536/1537 lived Tonkoi Onfilogov. Thus the family name Yurlov and the rare patronymic naming Onfilogov for the first time converge in one uyezd and one generation. But Inkovo and Priluki have not yet been brought into a single landholding complex, the wife of Ivan Menshoi has not been identified, and the transfer of Nikolskoye Svechino to Stefanida has not been traced. This is a strong line of research, not a proven identity.

WHO CREATED THE DOCUMENT. The survey was carried out by the sovereign's scribes Ivan Petrovich Zabolotsky and Mikhail Ivanov Usov-Tatishchev. Their names are not names of inhabitants of Onfilogovo: they designate officials who measured and recorded the lands of Tver uyezd on behalf of the authorities. The book was authenticated by the diak Semeika Karpov, and from l. 179 onwards by Andrei Myasnov. Since the article on Onfilogovo is on l. 183 ob.–184, Andrei Myasnov's counter-signature is particularly important for this section. These four names help to establish the origin of the record, but not the genealogy of the village.

HOW THE NAME IS FORMED. «Онфилогово» ["Onfilogovo"] consists of the personal stem Onfilog-, the possessive suffix -ov- and the neuter ending -o. The literal meaning is "Onfilog's settlement", "Onfilog's place" or "that which belongs to Onfilog". This is the same pattern as in the neighbouring names Sadykovo, Ishkovo, Ostrogino, Voronino and Popovo: the hamlets are named through their link to a person, but the grammatical form alone does not tell whether he was a peasant, a headman or an owner.

WHAT THE EPONYM WAS CALLED. The most reliably recoverable layer is the personal name Onfilog. The sources contain the closely related vernacular forms Anfilog, Anpilog, Ampilog and Amfilog: scribes rendered the unfamiliar church name by ear, and the initial Amf-, Anf-, Anp- and Onf- fluctuated. N. A. Petrovsky connects the forms Amfil and Amfilokh with the name Amfilokhy (Amphilochius). The onomastician V. A. Nikonov made an important correction: Amfil also existed as a separate canonical name, and in living speech derivatives of Amfilokhy, Amfil, Ampely and Amply could be mixed. Therefore the church form Amfilokhy is the most probable, but it is not proven as rigorously as the everyday name Onfilog.

WHAT THE FULL NAME COULD MEAN. If the original form really was the Greek Amphilochius, Petrovsky explains it through the Greek amphi — "around, on both sides" — and lochos — "ambush"; in the classical tradition Amphilochus is the personal name of a hero. But the meaning of the Greek prototype was not the meaning of the village name for 16th-century Tver inhabitants: for them Onfilogovo meant first of all "Onfilog's village", not "the village of one surrounded by an ambush".

THE NAME WAS REAL, NOT INVENTED FROM THE TOPONYM. The scribal book of Oryol uyezd of 1594/1595 names a former owner «Анпилогом Ивановым сыном Онаньина» ["Anpilog, son of Ivan, Onanyin"], the grandfather of the pomeshchik recorded at that time. The book does not give the exact time of his life and ownership. Ryazan sources know a peasant Anpilog, or Anfilog, son of Ivan, Konstantinov. These people are not the Tver founder and are not in any proven kinship with him, but they show that Anpilog/Anfilog was really used as a male personal name and could belong both to a service landholder and to a peasant.

WHEN THE TVER ONFILOG LIVED. By 1539/1540 the name had already become established, and the hamlet itself had four households. Consequently, the eponym lived before the first surviving survey. A cautious dating is the 15th or the very beginning of the 16th century; a more precise date is impossible until an earlier charter or a record of a transfer of ownership is found. Four households show an already formed hamlet, but do not allow its age to be calculated: it could have grown from a single household or new clearing (pochinok) within one or two generations, or it could have existed longer.

FOUR HOUSEHOLDS — WITHOUT NAMES. Not only the abridged printed text of 1877 has been checked, but also the digital image of the original RGADA book. The article begins on l. 183 ob. and continues on l. 184; there it indeed says «дер. Онфилогово: 4 дв.» ["hamlet of Onfilogovo: 4 households"], immediately followed by the ploughland and hay. There is no household-by-household list and no names of inhabitants. The unknown names of the four householders were not lost by the editor: the scribe himself did not record them. Therefore on this leaf it is impossible to pick one of the four peasants and declare him the founder.

WHO ONFILOG COULD HAVE BEEN. The most vivid scenario is a first settler or the head of a household around which the hamlet grew: a peasant cleared the land, set up a household, and the place came to be called by his name. But grammatically a headman, a minor service landholder or an earlier owner of the land are equally possible. Onfilogovo's position first in the list of six hamlets does not imply seniority and does not prove that it was the centre of the holding. The real Ryazan peasant Anfilog confirms the possibility of the peasant scenario, and the Oryol pomeshchik Anpilog that of the landowner scenario; it is not yet possible to choose between them for Tver.

THE FIRST NAMED HOLDER OF ANFILOGOVO ITSELF. In the official RGADA inventory for d. 16081, after 1634/1635, in the section on vacant lands of Yuryevsky stan, article No. 272 records «поместье Микиты Старкова, пустошь Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["the pomestye of Mikita Starkov, the waste land Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"]. Mikita is the old documentary form of the name Nikita; Starkov is the holder's family naming. He is not the founder: Onfilogovo existed at least 95 years before this entry, and under Mikita it was already counted as a waste land. But he is the first person found to whom, after Stefanida, the place itself belonged.

HOW STEFANIDA'S HOLDING BROKE UP. Neighbouring articles of the same inventory provide a control geography. Article No. 276 names Nikolskoye Svechino, Sadykovo and Ishkovo under Veriga Bulbin; article No. 310 names Voronino and Popovo under Semyon Yurlov. Five matching names within Yuryevsky stan prove that these are parts of a single complex of 1539/1540. By the 17th century it had been divided at least among Starkov, Bulbin and Yurlov, and the former village and hamlets are recorded as waste lands. Semyon's kinship with Ivan and Stefanida has not yet been proven.

THE SECOND NAME LEADS TO THE MODERN MAP. The formula «Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"] means two names of one place. The modern Beloglazovo in Zubtsov district lies only 2.42 km from the scholarly point of Nikolskoye Svechino and about 4 km from Pervitino. Therefore the marker has been moved to 56.316667, 35.242500 with high confidence; it shows the modern centre of Beloglazovo, not the exact sites of the four 16th-century households.

A LATER MAP PRESERVED THE HAMLET. On sheet 1–3 of the General Land Survey plan of Zubtsov uyezd, «д. Воронина» ["hamlet of Voronina"] and «д. Онфилогова» ["hamlet of Onfilogova"] can be read next to each other. This proximity is not accidental: Voronino and Onfilogovo were already in the same list of Stefanida's hamlets in 1539/1540. The label Onfilogova belongs to survey dacha No. 516. This for the first time traces the settlement from the 16th-century scribal book to a plan of the late 18th – early 19th century and gives a new address for research: the economic notes to dacha No. 516 should name its owner at that time, the number of households and the composition of the lands. Until the sheet is georeferenced with sufficient accuracy, the marker should not be presented as the exact site of the households.

WHAT IS PROVEN. In 1539/1540 Onfilogovo existed as a hamlet of four households attached to the village of Nikolskoye Svechino; it was assessed at 30 chetverts of ploughland in each of the three fields and hay meadows for 30 kopnas. The eponym was called by the everyday form Onfilog; his patronymic, social estate, occupation and exact lifetime are still unknown. The original record belongs to Yuryevsky stan of Khorvach volost. A scholarly GIS locates the centre of the Nikolskoye Svechino holding at 56.322586, 35.204732, and the General Land Survey plan (PGM) of Zubtsov uyezd separately shows the hamlet of Onfilogova next to the hamlet of Voronina, in dacha No. 516. The modern link to Beloglazovo is established by the double name and the landholding cluster; within the hamlet the exact sites of the 16th-century households have not been established. Kinship between the Tver Onfilog and the later Anfilogovs has not been established.
strings.Деревня Онфилогово в Юрьевском стане вол: The hamlet of Onfilogovo in Yuryevsky stan of Khorvach volost, Tver uyezd, is recorded in the scribal book of 7048 (1539/1540). Examination of the RGADA original on l. 183 ob.–184 confirmed the form of the name and the four households, but showed that the scribe did not record the names of the inhabitants. From the toponym the everyday name of the eponym — Onfilog — can be confidently reconstructed. Most likely this is a vernacular form of the name Amfilokhy (Amphilochius), although closely related forms could be mixed with the names Amfil, Ampely and Amply. A new land inventory after 1634/1635 for the first time continues the history of the place itself: in Yuryevsky stan, article No. 272 names «поместье Микиты Старкова, пустошь Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["the pomestye of Mikita Starkov, the waste land Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"]. The neighbouring articles distribute Stefanida's former holding between Veriga Bulbin and Semyon Yurlov. This confirms the identity of the settlement and shows its desertion, but does not make Mikita Starkov the founder: he appears about a century after the eponym.
strings.Генеалогически значимая часть записи рас: The genealogically significant part of the record has been transcribed.
strings.Современная привязка Онфилогова к Белогл: The modern link of Onfilogovo to Beloglazovo is established by the double name «Анфилогово, Белоглазово тож» ["Anfilogovo, also called Beloglazovo"] and the landholding cluster. Only the exact position of the four 16th-century households within the modern territory of the village has not been established.
strings.Не найдены экономические примечания к да: The economic notes to dacha No. 516 have not been found; it is they that should name the owner of Onfilogova in the era of the General Land Survey.
strings.Исповедная ведомость 1741 года содержит: The confession register (ispovednaya vedomost) of 1741 contains several identically named Nikolskoyes. The checked section on internal page 475 belongs to Zakhozhsky stan and is therefore not Nikolskoye Svechino of Volovitsky stan.
strings.В рукописном реестре тверской отказной к: In the manuscript register of the Tver transfer book (otkaznaya kniga) of 7176 (1667/1668), d. 16065, article No. 161, after a new examination of the enlarged official image, a different double name is read: «Анфилогово, Чагримово тож» ["Anfilogovo, also called Chagrimovo"]. It matches the separate hamlet of Onfilogovo, also called Chagrimovo, held by Stepan Afanasyevich Likharev in 1588. Therefore this four-leaf act has been excluded from the ownership chain of our Onfilogovo/Beloglazovo: the earlier readings «Филогово» ["Filogovo"] and «Дылово» ["Dylovo"] were palaeographic errors.
strings.В описи дела РГАДА 16089 найден тверской: In the inventory of RGADA case 16089 a Tver landholder, Rodion Punin syn Yurlov, who disputed a boundary in 1702, has been found. The six-leaf case itself has not yet been examined; his kinship with Ivan Yurlov and his relation to Nikolskoye Svechino have not been established.
strings.В селе Прилук Угличского уезда в 1536/15: In the village of Priluk in Uglich uyezd in 1536/1537 a monastery peasant, Tonkoi Onfilogov, is documented: he is recorded among the non-ploughing households of the votchina of the Trinity-Sergius Monastery. In the naming practice of this era the form «Онфилогов» ["Onfilogov"] primarily points to a father named Onfilog. This real Onfilog lived at a suitable time — probably at the turn of the 15th and 16th centuries. The geographical link is no longer reduced to distance alone: charters of 1461–1466 permitted the peasants and fishermen of the Priluki holding to pass through the Principality of Tver. However, neither the father nor Tonkoi is named in these charters, nor are they shown at Nikolskoye Svechino, so the candidate cannot yet be considered the founder.
strings.Родственная связь с орловскими Анфилогов: A kinship link with Oryol Anfilogovs has not been established and is probably absent.
strings.В данной 1567/1568 года найдено Острогин: In a deed of gift (dannaya) of 1567/1568, Ostrogino of Yuryevsky stan has been found, which the brothers Ivan and Matvei Timofeyevich Tsyzyrev sold to Stepan Oskolkov, who then gave it to the Iosif Monastery. It has not yet been established whether this is the same hamlet that in 1539/1540 was part of Stefanida's holding: the information on the Tsyzyrevs allows for the existence of a second identically named Ostrogino or of separate shares.
